[REDACTED]

incident_description:
I am reporting a safety concern regarding my Apple Watch.

While working out in my gym, I noticed that my Apple Watch started leaking a blue liquid onto my skin and clothing. It stained my T-shirt and left a large blue blotch on my thigh. I immediately went to the Apple Store Genius Bar at the [REDACTED] location in NYC, where I was assisted by an employee named [REDACTED].

[REDACTED] examined the watch and initially said, Well, there is no leaking right now, so there is nothing we can do. When I asked if this problem had ever been reported or if she was aware of it, she replied, Personally, I have never heard of it. I expressed concern that her response seemed dismissive. When I showed her similar cases found through an online search, she dismissed it by saying that was generative AI and not accurate.

I insisted that they address the issue. [REDACTED] said if I wanted to buy another watch, they could offer me a 10% discount. She brought over her manager, who told me they would file a safety concern report. I provided details about where the incident happened (a basement gym, not exposed to sunlight) and showed photos of the damage to my skin and clothing. [REDACTED] said I would receive a copy of the report  I have never received it and now assume it may never have been filed.

Later that week, Apple tech support called me ([REDACTED] from Texas) and requested photos. On the following Monday, [REDACTED] called again and told me it was just a water leak. When I asked why the liquid was blue, he said he wasnt a chemist but was sure it wasnt a battery leak because the screen wasnt broken. I also told him that one night the screen had felt cracked when I stepped outside in cold weather  but by the next morning, it appeared normal. [REDACTED] insisted that because the screen was intact and because the liquid amount appeared to be a lot in the photos, it could not be a battery leak. I questioned how he could determine the liquid amount from photos alone, but he stood by this conclusion.

Additionally, every time I touched the watch, I experienced a consistent heat or burning sensation on my finger. At first, I thought I might be imagining it, but it happened repeatedly.

While Apple has now asked me to send the watch in for repair, I feel that at every stage  especially at the store  I was stonewalled and not given proper assistance. [REDACTED] even tried to send me home initially, saying there was nothing they could do since the watch was no longer actively leaking.

I am filing this report because I believe this may represent a potential safety hazard involving the watchs battery or internal components, and I want this formally documented with the appropriate consumer protection authorities.
justification: The incident involved a leak of blue liquid from an Apple Watch onto the user's skin and clothing, causing staining and a burning sensation upon touch, but no severe injury was reported. The severity is rated as 3 (Injury) due to the skin irritation and burning sensation experienced by the user.

What Type of Product(s) Were Being Used?
		Product Name: Svanur Heated Jacket with Rechargeable Battery Pack

I was the sole user of the product. I am an adult male, and I was wearing the jacket in normal weather conditions while driving my car. Device was turne

How Were the Product(s) Being Used?

I was using the jacket normally and as intended driving my car while wearing it with the heating function turned OFF. The battery was not turned on when it caught on fire. The battery was properly connected inside the jackets designated battery pocket and had been fully charged two nights earlier.

Were There Any Injuries That Happened or May Have Happened While Using the Product?

Yes. I suffered severe burns on my abdomen when the battery burst into flames while inside the jacket. The fire burned through multiple layers of clothing and directly onto my skin before I was able to remove the jacket. The resulting fire also burned a hole in my car seat.

		The battery overheated and ignited spontaneously while inside the jackets battery pocket.

		I am now undergoing burn treatment, which includes applying prescription burn cream, keeping the area bandaged, and attending follow-up medical visits. I may require a skin graft surgery depending on how the wound heals.

Additional Notes:

		This accident could have been fatal if it had occurred while I was asleep. 
		I am concerned that this product poses a severe fire hazard to consumers, especially given how quickly the battery ignited during normal use. I had this jacket in my use for 3 months.

incident_description:
Subject: Request for Investigation and Recall of Apple Watch Bands Containing PFAS



Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to formally request that the Consumer Product Safety Commission investigate the health risks posed by certain Apple Watch bands due to the presence of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), as detailed in the recent study published in [REDACTED]. This study highlights significant concerns regarding dermal exposure to these forever chemicals, which are linked to severe health risks, including cancer, liver damage, and immune system disruption.

[REDACTED]

Background on the Study

The study analyzed 22 smartwatch wristbands, including those made from materials such as fluoroelastomers, which are commonly used in Apple Watch Sport Bands. Findings included:
	1.	High PFAS Concentrations:
Wristbands made from fluorinated synthetic rubber, such as fluoroelastomers, exhibited high levels of PFAS, specifically perfluorohexanoic acid (PFHxA).
	2.	Prolonged Skin Contact Risks:
The prolonged skin contact these bands facilitate may lead to dermal absorption of PFAS, a route of exposure that contributes to bioaccumulation and long-term health risks.
	3.	Carcinogenic and Toxic Effects:
PFAS have been linked to increased risks of cancer, liver toxicity, and immune system impairments, even at low levels of exposure.

Health and Safety Concerns

Apple has not publicly disclosed whether their watch bands contain PFAS, nor have they provided assurances regarding the safety of these materials for extended skin contact. Given the increasing evidence of the harmful effects of PFAS, this lack of transparency poses a significant risk to public health.

Request for Action

I respectfully request that the CPSC take the following actions:
	1.	Investigate:
Conduct a thorough investigation into the materials used in Apple Watch bands, particularly those made of fluoroelastomers.
	2.	Testing:
Require Apple to disclose detailed information regarding the chemical composition of their products and conduct independent testing to confirm the presence of PFAS.
	3.	Recall:
Issue a recall for affected products if they are found to contain harmful levels of PFAS.
	4.	Public Notification:
Ensure Apple provides clear information to consumers about the risks associated with PFAS in their products and offers safer alternatives.

Conclusion

Millions of consumers wear these bands daily, assuming they are safe. The CPSC has a critical role in protecting public health and safety, and I urge you to prioritize this issue. I am happy to provide additional information or support further investigation as needed.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involves potential health risks due to PFAS in Apple Watch bands, but no injury or death has been reported. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible due to the widespread use of these bands and the potential for dermal exposure.

incident_description:
I am writing to report a serious injury caused by a product sold at Clair's store as part of their piercing offerings.  My 10 year old daughter ended up in the Emergency Room on 08/04/24 after one of the earrings that were placed at a Clair's stores ended up stuck inside her earlobe.  Here is the timeline of events that led to this incident. 

My daughter [REDACTED] had her ears pierced on July 2nd at a Clair's Store at The Block in Orange in California.  The piercing procedure itself went well and did not cause any problems.  
However, after wearing the earrings for a month and following Clair's after care procedure, we attempted to take the earrings off.  [REDACTED] had been wearing the earrings for over one month at that point.  August 4, we attempted to remove the stud earrings.  The first one came out ok.  The second one on her left ear (facing her) was extremely tight and when we tried pull the two earring pieces apart, the rime stone part) front of earring) logged into her earlobe.  
We had to take her to the Emergency Room immediately as she was in a lot of pain due to the earring/rime stone (front piece of earring) being stuck in her earlobe.
We first took her to urgent care but doctor could not remove without just numbing gel on her ear.  The pain was too unbearable for my daughter when doctor tried to push earing out.  Urgent Care then sent us to ER.  At the ER, the ER doctor had to give her three shots to numb her ear, and then was finally able to remove the earring.
In looking at the earrings, I noticed that the quality of this earrings is terrible and should not be offered to kids that just have had their ears pierced. The earring causing the issue was way too tight where the two parts (back piece and the "pin part" of the earring come together), the "earring back piece" barely moves on the "needle piece".  The size of the rime stone is very small.  The combination of these two issues can easily cause the earring to get lodged in an earlobe, especially if still tender after piercing.  I went back to another Clair's store and looked at several stud earrings and they all had the same issue of the two pieces being very tight together and the back piece not being very movable on the pin.  This event was very traumatic on my daughter as well as myself.  These Clair's earrings are not safe and should not be offered to any other consumer, especially not children!
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury requiring medical attention, including a trip to the Emergency Room, indicating a significant harm. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible due to the design of the earrings and similar issues found in other earrings at the store.

incident_description:
Oriental Trading Company - Glow Swizzle Bracelet - Item #24/1442

On Saturday, 4/27/24, my 3-year-old son picked up this item from our entertainment console. He was not handling it in any aggressive fashion, but the item snapped and splashed its internal contents all over his face. He screamed in pain about his left eye. He set the glow stick back down on the table and the liquid oozed out and quickly deteriorated the varnish and paint within seconds (as pictured below). The smell of the liquid was overwhelming, like paint thinner. I immediately began cleaning his face and irrigating his eye the best I could, and contacted the Poison Control Center. They advised us to irrigate his eye for 15-30 minutes in the bathtub, which we did. The experience was very painful and traumatic for a child this age, as you can imagine. Given the clearly caustic nature of this liquid and its direct contact with my sons eye, we proceeded to the local Childrens ER to have him evaluated. They performed a few tests and thankfully, he appears to be OK. They advised that we follow up with a pediatric ophthalmologist to get the all-clear, and that visit is still pending.

This glow stick was obtained from a school function. Another parent reported to me that her son also had one break in his hand earlier that same day. He experienced a mild burning sensation from the liquid inside, and also noted the terrible smell.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a child, with the liquid from the glow stick causing pain and potential eye irritation, but no long-term damage was reported. The occurrence of similar incidents with the same product suggests that this was not an isolated event.

incident_description:
I purchased several items of clothing described online as 95% cotton an/or linen. When I got them, these seemed like polyester, but I thought it might be sizing, so I washed them. The texture changed and I thought they might be some kind of blend I'd be willing to wear. I trimmed a swatch from the seam of one garment in order to see what happened if I held a match to it, because that is an easy way to test for polyester in fabric (poly will melt along the edges). To my horror, the entire swatch burned very rapidly, with toxic black smoke, with residue of black melted plastic falling into the sink (of course I did this test over a sink). I don't want to see anyone wear this clothing. Contact with a match, cigarette, stove or candle could cause severe injury or death while wearing. The prints are beautiful and I would be terrified to ever wear them. I also don't want to give them away or return them to be sold to someone else. There is no fabric content label on the clothing itself, and the website states absolutely false information about the fabic content. I have no way of knowing if the seller knows that the fabric content is wrong. I am keeping these items for now in hopes that CPSC will test them more scientifically than I can. 
These are being sold by "Life Be Wonderful"
https://lifebewonderful.com/
service@newgodshop.com items listed on the website "comstylish.com"
The receiver of this payment is Non-US - Verified
justification: The fabric burned rapidly with toxic smoke and melted plastic when exposed to a flame, indicating a high risk of severe injury or death if worn and exposed to heat. The lack of accurate fabric content labeling and safety testing increases the risk of adverse incidents.

I have ridden on countless escalators with other similar luggage in countless countries, never having the slightest problem.  I'm strong and healthy.  However, with this newest suitcase, the wheel base expands as the suitcase expands, so I found myself on an up escalator near baggage claim at SEA (the Seattle, Washington airport), suddenly realizing the back two wheels would not fit on the escalator riser, so they were hanging over the edge, causing the 43-pound suitcase to tilt backwards. I'm not sure if I would have lived through such a fall, or if I had lived, if I would have sustained head, neck or back or other injuries or if I'd have been capable of walking again.  Had there been a crowded escalator, or one with small children or with parents holding infants or with elderly people, my fall might have set off a cascade of injuries.  But instead, there was only one person behind me, and he happened to be an able-bodied man in his 30s, who dropped his own suitcase, letting it fall to the bottom of the escalator, and he rushed up to me, said "I've got you," and held my shoulders and head and prevented me from falling any more until we arrived at the top and he helped me stand up. So I'm quite sore but alive and ambulatory, thanks to the fact that a good Samaritan came to my rescue.  But I think the fact that the wheel base expands with the suitcase expansion is a hazard and an accident waiting to happen.  I fear others may not be as lucky as I was and they could suffer far worse injuries or even die as a result of such an unstable situation. I hope you will reconsider this luggage "feature." This letter is a written notification and description of a severe injury caused to my eye by a metal tipped elastic hood drawstring. The drawstring was on the hood of a jacket labeled by Kenneth Cole. A photograph of the jacket label is attached. On December 3rd, 2019, I wore the Kenneth Cole jacket on my commute home from work, in Chicago by train. At the end of my return trip home, I stood up to exit the train. As I stood up and walked from my seat, the elastic drawstring of the hood of the jacket was held in the seam of the train seat cushion. When I turned to look at
where the drawstring was stuck it snapped into my face. The metal tip of the drawstring hit my eye, propelled at high speed by the slingshot action of the elastic cord. I immediately felt immense sharp pain and lost vision in my eye. I needed assistance to exit the train. When I was off the busy train, I called my husband. He came to pick me up and take me to the hospital.

At the hospital I was treated in the emergency room. My eye had extreme damage from the impact of the metal tip of the drawstring. I was bandaged and given eyedrops and pain medication. I have had multiple follow-up treatments for my retina, cornea, and a Lasik doctor; I've also had to undergo a cataract surgery. My vision is still not repaired, and I will need a 2nd surgery. The vision in my right eye is currently 300/20; and before this accident, it was 20/20. My right eye pupil is permanently dilated and disfigured. My eyesight is impaired. I now have a permanent disability of my vision because of the Kenneth Cole Jacket. A photo of my injured eye is attached.

I am sending this notice to the Manufacture and the Government to request a recall all jackets with hard tipped elastic drawstrings. [REDACTED]

[REDACTED], the Kenneth Cole Jacket that injured me should not have been made and it should have been recalled to prevent my injury. It was known by the Government and the clothing industry that hoods with elastic draw cords cause injuries. Yet, the Kenneth Cole Jacket with its hard tipped elastic drawstring continued to be sold.

The purpose of this notice is to immediately prevent more eye injuries like mine from happening. I reserve the right to seek compensation for my injury. Please respond that you have received this injury notice letter from me.

Thank You,

I am a 78 woman and have 3 pairs of Skechers shoes. The first pair I got years ago and wore a lot. I think they were Skechers Go Walk slip ins. Very comfortable. It wasn't until maybe last year that I started having the problem described by many of the people who posted at this website:
[REDACTED]
I didn't know the word to use to explain what was happening, but it started happening more frequently - sticking, catching on the floor (or outdoors or on carpet). I figured they were getting worn out. So I decided not to wear them outside any more. Then on March 21, 2021, I was wearing them in my kitchen (in my apartment) (on a composite wood floor) and I was exercising, doing side steps and the next thing I knew, what people describe as 'catching the front of the shoe' happened and I went down really hard. I landed on the floor and thought for sure I had broken something. I am sure I was in shock as I lay there for awhile and then decided I had to see if I could move and get up. I was alone and my phone was on the kitchen counter, so if I was badly injured I couldn't have gotten help because the walls are so well insulated where I live, no one would have ever heard me screaming. It was terrifying. I was able to move myself to a carpeted area and managed to get up off the floor. I was terribly shaken and sore. I had fallen on my left side and hit the top of my thigh/hip area and my left side and left forearm, hand and thumb were starting to hurt quite a lot. Luckily I was able to walk. I iced the areas. It took several weeks for the pain to go away. At first I couldn't even use my hand and the hip area was painful too. Then I got black and blue from my hip bone down to the middle of my thigh and my hand and arm were black and blue also. I was very lucky! I immediately threw away the old Skechers. But I already had two other pairs - one is Skechers GOGA MAX and the other newest pair is Skechers Air Cooled GOGA MAT. I have been wearing them but then noticed that the catching at the front causing me to almost trip happened with those too. I figured it was just me, but I wondered if anyone else had this problem. Today, when it happened, I [REDACTED] "Skechers fall" and found this site and I am really angry to know this has happened to other people! I could have broken my hip or hit my head! I'm not sure what to do about this now that I know I am not the only one. I know I will not continue to wear my Skechers, much as I love them and will not ever buy them again. I shudder to think of myself and how many countless others have injured themselves and may not know how dangerous these shoes are.

incident_description:
Burned by my Apple Watch 4:

I purchased a new Apple Watch directly from Apple on 9/15/18, and received the watch on 9/26.  I wore it happily and without incident until 2/19/19.  I went for a run on the afternoon of 2/18/19 with my Apple Watch as usual.  I didnÃÂt notice anything unusual with the watch and didn't do anything  unusual with the watch.  I took a shower with it on when I got home, cleaned and the inside of the band and the back of it after my shower and put it on the charger for ~4-5 hours.  I put it back on when just before I went to bed because I use it as an alarm clock because there is a setting that wakes you by vibration rather than by an audible alarm.  I woke on 2/19/19 and didnÃÂt really notice specific discomfort as I rushed to get ready for work.  While walking the dog, I did notice that my wrist felt sensitive under my watch and just felt odd.  When I got to work, I felt discomfort and a burning sensation.  I took off the watch and noticed red marks that looked like a first degree burn.  I left the watch off, and the burn continued to worsen over the next 24 hours.  It blistered, and the blister ultimately popped.  As of 2/22/19 there is still redness (especially where the blister was where there is now a sore), but it is healing.

I initiated a chat with Apple via their website on 2/20 to report the issue.  The representative set up an appointment for me to talk to someone in Safety the next day.  The next day (2/21) someone from the Technology trouble shooting team called, and then they connected me with [REDACTED] from Apple's Safety team.  [REDACTED] was very friendly and collected the above information and asked many other questions.  I explained that I never felt a burning sensation so bad that I had to rip the watch off.  I explained that it seemed like it partially happened while I slept during the night of 2/18-19, and partially on the morning on 2/19 when I felt the burning/discomfort sensation.   

[REDACTED] sent me a link and asked me to upload photos of the watch and my wrist to an Apple Customer Service site.  I did so on 2/21.  On 2/22 [REDACTED] called to follow up.  He stated that he had not yet read the report from the technical team, did so in less than a minute with me on the line and stated that the determination was that the injury could not have come from a burn.  He said that it was consistent with a reaction to the watch materials.  He also stated that I am not eligible for a refund (despite having purchased the Apple Care Warranty) ÃÂ and stated that the problem is with me and my skin and how it reacts to the materials in the watch as opposed to a problem with the materials in the watch or overheating.  

There are quite a few similar complaints on Apple's own discussion sites (along with pictures), and similar stories reported in the media.  However, Apple has still not issued a recall, and does not seem to be taking the issue seriously.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn injury, classified as a severity level of 3. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely, as the user had previously worn the watch without incident and similar complaints are reported but not widespread.

incident_description:
We had an unused plastic Nautica beach umbrella that we had purchased from Sam's Club on March 10, 2018. It was the second day of using it at the beach. There was a slight wind, but everyone's umbrellas on the beach were doing fine. We were relaxing under the umbrella when suddenly I felt the upper half of the umbrella wack my head and nose. The upper half of the umbrella had slid out of its "secured" holding position, held down by the traditional two tightening clips, and flown down with force upon my face. Three days later I still have a bruise on my head and still gives me a headache when I check that area or touch it too much.

We observed the umbrella over the course of the next few days and observed that any wind at all would slowly pull it out of its secured holding position. We finally had to duck tape it to hold it in place so we wouldn't get clobbered again (This is shown in photo--sorry, unable to upload). The design is a potential hazard for other customers who have the same product and a definite hazard for us. I can literally pull the pole out of its holder even though it is "secured".

It is also worth noting that after only 4 days of use the twist bottom shows signs of stress on the plastic, which indicates it could break rather soon, and potentially cause another hazard. And also around the screws of the tightening clips are stress marks. (These are shown in photos--sorry, unable to upload.)

The product label says it is a Nautica Classic Teal distributed by Essex Mfg, Inc at 350 Fifth Ave NY NY 10118-3299 and the # below the barcode reads: 0-1265501926-9 (the 0 and 9 are before and after the barcode--not sure if they are  applicable).
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, as evidenced by a bruise on the head and headaches. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible, given the design flaw and observed stress marks on the product.

We were discharged at 48 hours at 5% weight loss with next-day follow-up.  We were told by the lactation consultant before discharge that he would be hungry and we were instructed to just keep putting him on the breast.  Upon getting home, he became fussy and I nursed him longer and longer into the night.  He cried even after nursing and latched back on immediately.  He did not sleep.  By the next morning, he stopped crying and was quiet.  We saw our pediatrician at around 68 hours of life (end of day 3).  Despite producing the expected number of wet and dirty diapers, he had lost 1 pound 5 ounces, about 15% of his birth weight. At the time, we were not aware of and were not told the percentage lost, and having been up all night long trying to feed a hungry baby, we were too exhausted to figure out that this was an incredible amount of weight loss.  He was jaundiced but no bilirubin was checked.  Our pediatrician told us that we had the option of either feeding formula or waiting for my milk to come in at day 4 or 5 of life.  Wanting badly to succeed in breastfeeding him, we went another day unsuccessfully breastfeeding and went to a lactation consultant the next day who weighed his feeding and discovered that he was getting absolutely no milk.  When I pumped and manually expressed, I realized I produced nothing. I imagined the four days of torture he experienced and how 2 days of near-continuous breastfeeding encouraged by breastfeeding manuals was a sign of this. We fed him formula after that visit and he finally fell asleep. Three hours later, we found him unresponsive. We forced milk into his mouth, which made him more alert, but then he seized. We rushed him to the emergency room. He had a barely normal glucose (50 mg/dL), a severe form of dehydration called hypernatremia (157 mEq/L) and severe jaundice (bilirubin 24 mg/dL).  We were reassured that he would be fine, but having done newborn brain injury research, knowing how little time it takes for brain cells to die due to hypoglycemia and severe dehydration, I did not believe it, although I hoped it.

At 3 years and 8 months, our son was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder with severe language impairment. He has also been diagnosed with ADHD, sensory processing disorder, low IQ, fine and gross motor delays and a seizure disorder associated with injury to the language area of the brain. 

In the September, 2015 issue of Hospital Pediatrics, an article was published describing 11 exclusively breastfed newborn babies who developed profound hypoglycemia between the second and fifth day of life from insufficient breast milk intake.  The child described in the body of the article was a healthy full-term baby who presented just like my son.  He was seen on the third day of life at his pediatricianÃÂs office.  Despite that, he was found on the fourth day of life lethargic and unable to feed.  He had lost 10% of his birth weight and had a low glucose of 20 mg/dL (normal > 47 mg/dL).  This child was given IV glucose after which he developed a seizure.  They obtained a brain MRI which showed extensive areas of injury to almost the entire brain.  In addition to this child, 10 other healthy term newborns were identified to have developed hypoglycemia from insufficient breastfeeding as well. They were found lethargic, seizing, hypothermic and/or not breathing.  5 out of the 6 MRIs obtained in these babies showed widespread injury to a third to almost the entire brain in varying patterns.  They subsequently developed long-term neurological disabilities including seizure disorders, motor weakness, visual impairment and feeding difficulties requiring speech therapy."
justification: The incident led to severe health complications, including brain injury, and the baby's death was averted only by medical intervention. The severity is classified as 4 (Death) due to the life-threatening conditions and long-term disabilities described.

incident_description: Infant was wearing rattle socks which have a rattle in the shape of a bunny stitched onto the socks. She was wearing them while in the back seat of the car on the way to daycare. When we arrived I noticed she had removed one of the socks, so I put it back on without looking closely at it. Just as I was leaving her, I noticed something white in her mouth. On closer examination, she had pulled off the ear of the bunny - about the size of a dime - and had it in her mouth. She must have had it in her mouth for at least 5-10 minutes, and it was large enough to block her airway if she'd tried to swallow it. I took off her socks to examine them and saw that the stitches holding the ear to the bunny head had ripped, which were also the stitches keeping the stuffing and rattle disk inside. The stuffing was now coming out, and if she had continued chewing on the sock while in the back seat, she easily could have swallowed the stuffing and the rattle disk (slightly larger than a dime) as well. None of the stitching on the socks is very solid - the stitching of ears to animal head, the stitching holding in the stuffing and rattle disk, and the stitching holding the rattle to the sock - and an infant could easily pull off/pull apart the different components and choke. On November 25, 2015, I purchasedÃÂ Warner's No Side Effects Lace Underwire Bra in Black from a KohlÃÂs store in Santa Rosa, CA. A few weeks later, I wore it for the first time. I forgot to wash the bra before wearing it, as I had with the other No Side Effects bras I purchased on the same day. 

In a few hours, the bra caused so much itching I had to remove it. When I did, I found a red rash and raised, red bumps in exactly the shape of the bra, down to the lines of the shoulder straps. Other bumps had a hard, white, almost fluid looking center surrounded by red margins, and were hard as gravel. By the following morning, the rash had spread to my torso, back, and upper chest. Fortunately, I thought to take photos to track its progression and healing.

I treated the rash by taking [REDACTED], applying [REDACTED] cream multiple times a day, everything I could think of. Nothing worked. The itching was so maddening I scratched my skin open and could not sleep at night. Multiple times each night, I would get up and apply cold washcloths followed by [REDACTED] cream, in an attempt to calm the rash down enough to be able to fall asleep. 

During the day, it was almost unbearable to have fabric next to my skin, and I could not stand to wear any bra at all. As I own and operate my own business, this lack of sleep and discomfort with clothing made focus on work and visits to client sites particularly challenging.

After about two weeks of this, with no improvement in the rash, I saw a dermatologist at a local research university. He ordered blood work and took a 4mm core biopsy of one of the hard, white bumps, as he said heÃÂd never seen anything like it before. He also prescribed a strong topical steroid that has helped somewhat but, four weeks later, the rash and maddening itching remain. Soon, we should have more information on what the rash is and, hopefully, what may have caused it. 

Previously, I have never had a rash. I have never had any skin problems ÃÂ no rashes, eczema, acne, nothing of the sort. 

With the help of a scientist friend, I have found two textile testing labs where I will pay to send segments of the bra to be tested for whatever may be in and/or on them. 

Buyer beware with these bras. I would not wish this experience on anyone.
justification: The incident caused a severe skin rash, itching, and discomfort, resulting in injury. The likelihood of occurrence appears unlikely as this was a singular event experienced by the individual.

incident_description:
It was New YearÃÂs Eve 2014 and I was wearing a lululemon sweatshirt while sitting against a pillow on my couch.  When I got up I unknowingly pinched the elastic hood tie between my hand and the couch and when it was at full stretch it shot back directly into my left eye.  The pain was immediate and intense as the end of the tie was metal and as such hit me very hard.  I covered my eye as it felt as though the eyeball would fall out of the orbital cavity.  Upon removing my hand once in front of a mirror I could not see from the injured eye and with my functional eye identified blood coming from near the iris and dripping out of the eye onto my face.  I phoned my mother who is a pediatric anesthesiologist and she was concerned for the integrity of the eye.  She phoned the local ED and the physician on duty said I could wait and come in first thing in the morning as it was a busy evening with NYE revelers.
?At 6:00am 1.1.2015 I checked into Swedish Emergency Department in Seattle, Washington.  I met with [REDACTED] who diagnosed me with a subconjunctival hemorrhage and sent me home with some eye drops and a prescription for Aleve twice daily until the pain subsided.  That morning I attempted to go to work but the pain was too strong and I had to find a replacement.  The following day, 1.2.2015, my pain was the same if not more so and the photosensitivity I had experienced initially was much greater, leaving me no choice but to conduct myself with the left eye closed at all times.  I visited an [REDACTED] an ophthalmologist at Eye Associates Northwest who concurred with [REDACTED]assessment but did note I had worsening vision and sent me home with a cover for my eye as it healed over the next few days.

Due to the horrific nature of the way my eye looked, as well as the pain in which I found myself, I was out of work for several days, for a total of 31 paid and tipped hours.  When I was finally able to get back to work the humiliation of an eye fully engulfed in blood was a lot to bear.  I work in service and dancing around what people saw on my face was a delicate and uncomfortable matter.

After 13 days the blood was nearly drained from the eye and my pain was minimal.  I did stay on a regimen of Aleve for 3 weeks after the injury.?
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, specifically a subconjunctival hemorrhage, which caused pain, vision issues, and temporary disability. The unusual and accidental nature of the incident suggests it is rare.

incident_description:
I was leaving a residence and stepped off of a wooden porch onto a slightly sloped concrete walkway.  Upon taking the third step on the walkway with my left foot, I felt my ankle began to turn causing me to lose my balance and fall forwardÃÂ I tried to shuffle my feet to regain my balance, as I have done before in similar situations, but this time I seemed to be thrust forward at an accelerated rate - almost like someone was pushing me.  I knew I was going to fall face forward on the concrete, so I put out both arms to protect my face and head ÃÂ I fell at such an angle that my right hand and arm took most of the forceÃÂ 
     As I regained my senses, I tried to raise myself off the concrete but immediately knew something was wrong, as pain shot up my right arm into my shoulder, and I could NOT push up with my right armÃÂ So, I was forced to roll around on the concrete until I could use my left arm to help me struggle to my knees, which by now were burning and throbbing ÃÂ but not nearly as much as my arm.  I tried to stand and almost fell again because I realized my left ankle was hurting and the shape of the soles of the shoes made it harder to stand, but I managed to get my balance and walk to my vehicleÃÂ
    My right arm began to stiffen and swell immediately, and it was almost impossible to bend my right arm... I didn't know the full extent of my injuries until I arrived home nearly 20 minutes later, and I could barely walk or get undressed.  My right arm had swollen dramatically, my left ankle was swelling and both knees and the palms of both hands were bleeding from abrasions from the concrete when I fell... My roommate wanted to take me to the Emergency Room immediately, but because I did not have insurance, I suffered through a terribly painful night until an Urgent Care clinic nearby opened the next morning... 
    Upon examination, the Dr. on call at the clinic IMMEDIATELY referred me to a surgeon... I was scheduled that day for surgery as X-rays showed both bones in my right forearm were broken just below my elbow... I was put on pain medication and scheduled for surgery as soon as possible - a titanium plate and two screws were required to repair the break(s), and I was without use of my right arm (my dominant arm) for nearly 3 months... I slowly regained the use of my right arm, but still (almost 5 yrs later) cannot fully straighten my arm and I have just recently regained MOST of my strength and almost full use of that arm...
    These shoes are marketed as "Fitness Footwear" that was designed to "improve your life by changing the way you walk" and the enclosed literature states: "Shape Ups are designed to enhance the benefits of walking by stimulating muscles not utilized with standard walking shoes"....  This made these shoes very attractive to someone like me, who had suffered for years with chronic pain, swelling and stiffness in my lower legs, feet and ankles - making walking difficult and painful... I enthusiastically bought these expensive shoes (on sale for $110.00) because I wanted to start walking again and needed to do so as painlessly and efficiently as possible - these shoes seemed to fit the bill.
    However, there is NO TYPE of WARNING within any literature about these shoes that states the added height and cushioning of the shoe design made them unstable over uneven surfaces - even small cracks in sidewalks, pebbles on the ground or other loose impediments could potentially cause a person to easily lose his/her balance... The ONLY warning is that: "due to this unconventional manner of walking, we suggest you moderate your walking routine in Shape Ups for the first week or two (25 to 45 minutes per day), depending on your level of fitness... NOTHING ELSE...
    The highly anticipated blessing and relief the design of these shoes promised, has turned into a nightmare for me... Not only did I endure excruciating pain for several days, the damaged caused by my fall cost me over $13,000.00 in medical expenses (which I am still trying to pay off... PLUS, it has taken me almost the all the nearly 5 yrs. since my fall to regain MOST of the strength, full use a flexibility I had in my right arm before - and I will probably NEVER be able to fully straighten it again and I STILL periodically experience throbbing pain and weakness in my right arm....
    Although I like the shoes (for the most part) that Skechers USA puts out (and have bought 3 pairs of other, more "conventional styles"), I feel they have EGREGIOUSLY FAILED consumers such as myself who bought in to the promise of a "more comfortable and enhanced" way of obtaining the health benefits of walking, by not warning us of the possible instability this shoe design presents novice users.... 
    I paid a painful, heavy price for this FAILURE - NO ONE ELSE SHOULD...
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, including a broken forearm requiring surgery and long-term rehabilitation. The injury was caused by the design of the shoes, which made the user lose balance and fall.

I showered in my main-floor bathroom, seated on a hospital chair in the tub, with a plastic bag (from toe to knee) over my Velcro-fastened cast. I went through three months of physical therapy for rehabilitation.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, including a double ankle break and dislocation requiring surgery and a lengthy recovery period. The likelihood of such an incident occurring is unlikely, as it involved a specific accident while wearing slip-resistant shoes.

incident_description:
I injured my wrist on March 18, 2011 while wearing Skechers Shape Up shoes.  I was walking to the store near my house. I cut through a grassy area near a basketball court. It had been raining so the ground was wet and muddy.  When I reached an area that was particularly muddy I attempted to turn to step out of it; when I lost my footing and fell.
I returned to my home and a friend took me to the ER the next day.  They stabilized my wrist but did not surgery.  The orthopedic surgeon on duty told me to see him in his office in two days.  When I went there he would not see me because I was un insured.  I made many calls to find a surgeon who would treat me without insurance.  I also tried unsuccessfully to apply for medical assistance and disability.  After six weeks I located the Union Memorial Hospital program that provides care for un insured individuals.  I was evaluated there and it was determined that at this point my wrist had healed incorrectly and to fix it would require surgery for re breaking and setting.  Next I had to apply for their program and it took another six weeks for approval.  When I received approval I was immediately scheduled for surgery in July 2011. They placed hardware inside to set my wrist.  Following surgery I was seen periodically for evaluation and occupational therapy.  In October 2011 I underwent a second surgery to remove the hardware.  This was followed by more evaluation and therapy for four more months.  I was discharged in February 2012.  I learned about the Skechers class action lawsuit in June 2012 and submitted my information to it.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the wrist, requiring medical attention and subsequent surgeries. The likelihood of such an incident occurring is unlikely, as it involved a specific combination of factors including wet and muddy ground and a loss of footing.

incident_description:
In February of 2014 I purchased a pair of Dr. Scholl's Escape (2522966) walking shoes in anticipation of being on my feet a lot during a couple week trip to England for work. Very comfortable nice fitting shoes I wore the shoes a lot sightseeing when not working. However after the second week I noticed some reddening and peeling of the skin on top of both feet and a few days later the same on the bottoms but much worse. Thought maybe it was athlete's foot or a fungus from the motel shower or carpet so I began applying antifungal cream to both feet. Thinking all was well and the problem would go away I continued to wear the shoes, after a while the skin on both feet on the tops and bottoms had started to crack and peel and had this burned appearance. Kept up with the cream and wearing the shoes thinking it would just take a while to clear up. After returning home to the states, my wife was shocked by the condition of my feet, the entire tops and bottoms of both feet were discolored (reddish brown to almost black areas) and looked like they had been burned. Then the peeling began the tops and bottoms of both feet completely peeled off several times at one point the pain was so intense I couldn't hardly even walk and if I did the pain was excruciating. I went to the doctor and he said it was some kind of contact dermatitis and prescribed a cortisone cream which seemed to help, but it was the end of April before my feet were back to normal. During this time I had not done a lot of walking so I had not worn my "walking" shoes. Then the weekend of June 1 2014 I and my wife went to a local car show and being as I was going to be walking for several hours I wore my aforementioned "walking" shoes. The next morning noticed that that once again my feet looked as if they had been burned, and by mid week had started to crack and peel again. Not as bad as before but I only had the shoes on for a few hours instead of days and days.
This hardly seemed like a coincidence and thats when it occurred to me that it was the shoes causing the problem. Last week I saw a post on Facebook about a woman who had purchased some flip flop sandals from Wal-Mart that were made in China and that the materials and dyes they used caused major burning on her feet that looked just like my feet did and that made me think. My shoes were from Wal-Mart and as you can guess also made in China. Coincidence? I'm thinking not.
Not sure about contacting an Attorney. Any suggestions?
justification: The incident caused significant skin irritation, cracking, and peeling on both feet, resulting in pain and discomfort, which aligns with a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely (2) as the reaction seems specific to the shoes and not a common issue reported elsewhere.

incident_description:
On 5/2/2014, I was home for lunch and preparing for an overnight trip.  I picked up my two Saddleback leather satchels (medium and large sized) by the shoulder straps to take them out to my car.  As I got the strap for the large bag to shoulder height and prepared to place the strap on my shoulder, the heavy metal clasp that connects the strap to the bag disconnected from the side of the bag facing forward.  This caused a weighted pendulum effect, swinging the strap up from the bag towards my face, with the metal clasp violently striking me in the teeth and loosening my four upper front teeth and causing them to hurt badly.

I have a number of Saddleback bags, and have had the clasps disconnect a number of times in the past due to the design, but never had the strap strike me before.  It has always been clear to me since the first incident that these straps need to have more than a latching mechanism - they need a latching AND locking mechanism.  However, it never occurred to me that the disconnecting clasp issue could cause bodily harm in addition to possibly damaging the contents of the bags.  

I no longer feel safe picking up my bags as intended as a result of this.  I contacted Saddleback via their web contact form that I have used in the past and previously gotten replies in a couple hours.  They have not replied in the two days that have passed.  In the meantime, in order to use my bags and feel I can do so safely, I have tied the clasps to the bags with para-cord.  I do no feel this is a good long term solution since these bags are expensive and supposedly warrantied for 100 years.  I had also never thought it was possible to be beat up by a bag before, but now I know it can happen with these bags.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, as the metal clasp struck the person's teeth, loosening four upper front teeth. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as this was an isolated incident and despite past issues with the clasp design, it had not previously caused bodily harm.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while wearing the jeans in a heated seat in the car, she started feeling uncomfortably hot and itchy.  She got home and removed the jeans, she noticed that she had broke out in hives and had large welts in her genital area, even areas where the jeans were not touching.  She had to treat herself with [REDACTED].  No medical attention was received.  She had wore the jeans several times before, however, lately she noticed that she had been itching whenever it was worn.

12/30/13 The manufacturer was contacted and she was advised that there was no formaldehyde in the product and that they had not received any complaints on this issue.  She was informed that it could have been from the dye.

She feels that these jeans are a health hazard and should be reported.

UPDATE FROM CONSUMER:
When I called the manufacturer and talked with the receptionist I said I thought I was having an allergic reaction to a pair of their pants. The receptionist immediately said, "Oh, with a pair of blue jeans?" I said yes and she said she thought so. When I talked to a company representative I was told they hadn't had any other complaints. If that were true I asked the company representative why the receptionist immediately guessed that the problem was my blue jeans. The company representative then said the receptionist shouldn't have said that, but offered no explanation.

I told the company representative that the jeans were stretch denim and that I didn't have any problems with [REDACTED] or spandex in other clothes. Therefore I felt my allergic reaction was due to the dye. The company representative said the only complaint it had had with its jeans was an odor. It determined the odor was caused by the dye being incorrectly mixed at one time, and the problem was corrected.

My jeans did not have an odor, but after just one wearing the dye was wearing off on the upper portion of the legs. You can see this in the photo.  I had been itching a lot and thought it was due to dry skin or my wool socks. It wasn't until I was  wearing my pants on a car's seat warmer that I had an intense allergic reaction. I told the CPSC representative that I
had had a similar reaction of hives while wearing blue jeans once before. It was while I was sitting in bleachers at a baseball game. The heat from the sun made my blue jeans uncomfortably hot. I felt as if my skin were being burned. I have worn blue jeans all my life and have had them become warm in the sun, but this was far beyond anything I had ever before
experienced. I thought the increased heat was due to the dark color of the blue jeans. After the baseball game I  mmediately took the jeans off and my thighs were beet red and blotchy. I thought they were burned, but in hindsight I think I had hives. 

When I initially called CPSC I was thinking that the reaction at the baseball game was caused by a different pair of jeans - a pair made by the same manufacturer as the second pair, but by a different branch of the company - Lee Riders (purchased at Fleet Farm in Woodstock, IL). The second pair was made by Riders by Lee (purchased at Wal-Mart in Lake Zurich, IL). VF Corporation told me they are totally separate companies. I was told they don't use the same fabrics
or dyes. I am now unsure if the reactions were caused both times by the second pair of pants or if the first
one was caused by Lee Riders and the second reaction was due to the Riders by Lee. I still have both pairs and
would be willing to send them in for testing.

Two days after my severe reaction to the jeans, I wore them again for a few minutes and began to itch, not just on my legs, but all over. I then realized that the itching I had been experiencing lately was from my blue jeans, not dry skin, and not from wearing wool socks! I am also quite sure that I could reproduce the hive reaction by sitting on a car's seat warmer again and I would be willing to do so, to prove this product is faulty.

After I told the Riders by Lee and the VF Corporation representatives that I was going to contact the CPSC, I immediately received a call from Wrangler, which must be another division of VF Corporation. The Wrangler representative wanted me to send him the jeans and wanted to reimburse me. He wasn't pleased when I told him I would not be accepting any money or mailing him the jeans, since I would no longer have any evidence and the CPSC may want the jeans. I am not looking for compensation I would like to learn what it is that I am reacting to so I can avoid it in the future. I would also like to prevent anyone else from developing hives as I did.
justification: The consumer experienced an allergic reaction with symptoms of hives and large welts, indicating an injury. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible as the consumer had a similar reaction previously and was able to reproduce the itching sensation.

http://www.orgbyvio.com/shop/#!/~/product/category=2398135&id=18019823

"The huayruro* seed is a good luck seed. The red and black colors symbolize good fortune and abundance, as well as balance. The seeds are said to protect from negativity and bring happiness. Newborns and newlyweds often receive huayruro seeds as gifts for a happy and prosperous life."

They are poisonous. Nowhere on the page does it mention that they are poisonous.

Again, the website URL is:

http://www.orgbyvio.com/shop/#!/~/product/category=2398135&id=18019823
justification: The incident involves poisonous seeds being used in jewelry without warning, and the advertisement encourages giving them to newborns, posing a high risk of injury. incident_description: In Jan or Feb of 2012 I purchased a pair of FILA sculpt & tone shoes from Ross.  They were very comfortable and I ended up wearing them as everyday shoes.  Over spring break I began experiencing pain in my right hip.  I had recently begun walking more and thought it was due to that.  Over the summer it got so bad I had to go to an orthopedic specialist who injected cortisone into my hip and sent me to physical therapy.  The physical therapist felt the problem was originating in my back and pelvis rather than my hip.  I did get better but not all the way.  I ended up having an MRI in November for which my out of pocket cost was 900 dollars, but nothing could be diagnosed from it.  My hip has slowly been getting worse again, and finally last week my supervisor mentioned in passing that the shape up shoes were apparently hurting people.  I went online to check and sure enough, there are numerous complaints of woman suffering the same symptoms I am.  I can only hope that now that I know the source of the pain I'll be able to heal without further medical intervention.  I'll never wear that pair of shoes again.
justification: The incident involved hip pain and required medical intervention, including cortisone injections and physical therapy, indicating an injury. The likelihood of occurrence appears likely given the numerous complaints from women suffering similar symptoms.

At first we though one of the shoes was just defective and put another pair on our daughter then we literally heard that next pair break.  We inspected the shoes on our other daughter and saw it was cracking as well.   The shoes cracked along the middle, heal, and toe areas.  The cracks were sharp and jagged but fortunately, my daughters were not hurt.  They cried because they wanted to wear the shoes and thought they were responsible for breaking them.

The pain worsened and swellings and stiffness set in. Finally, I saw an orthopedic surgeon on 01/28/2013. He advises I that I have patella-femoral syndrome. incident_description:
I bought a pair of Skechers' Shake-Up shoes on Aug 18th, 2012. I had worn them for 3 months (from Sept 2012 to Nov 2012). Skechers used to claim their Shake-Up shoes can help to build your body. However, these shoes didn't work as they advertised and they cost permanent damage to my feet. During those three months, I used those shoes primarily for running and walking. Occasionally, I played Volleyball (around 4 times) in those shoes. Now I am diagnosed with Osteoarthritis on my big left toe. Osteoarthritis is rare among young adult (I'm 27 years old). My condition is definitely a result of wearing those shoes since I was extremely healthy before wearing those shoes and I had no injures on my foot before whatsoever. My life has changed dramatically after diagnosed with Osteoarthritis. I can't go to gym, play sports and hang out with friends like I used to do any more. Even walking now is a pain. My doctor says there is no treatment for my condition except surgery. However, surgery is not recommended at this stage considering I can still walk (even though in pain). Osteoarthritis can only gets worse with age and eventually a surgery is inevitable. I have already spent hundreds of dollars seeking treatment but there is no positive response from the doctors I saw. I am also worried about the surgery expense that I will have to to cover in near future which I couldn't afford for sure. 

I am devastating now and everything has changed after wearing those shoes. I feel disappointed with Schechers because they misled their customers and I doubt if they had run reliable experiments on their Shake-Up shoes before putting them into market. I feel Skechers should be responsible (at least partially) for what I am experiencing now and should take further action to prevent this from happening on any of their customers.
justification: The incident resulted in a diagnosed injury of Osteoarthritis, which is a clear indication of an injury. The likelihood of this specific injury occurring is rare, as it is uncommon among young adults.

incident_description:
I was ready to go home after helping my grandmother with parkinsons who lives in Marshfield.  My aunt was driving me home.  We were outside and I was walking down the outside stairs . I was on the last step to the bottom and my foot went in and I fell, breaking my tibia and fibula. I was wearing skechers shapeups which I got as an early birthday present and I was wearing them for the first day.  The first words out of my mouth were"these stupid shoes!" I also knew something was wrong because my leg didn't look right. Every little move I made I could hear the bones making a crackling noise. I had to hold it until the ambulance came in Marshfield and they brought me to South Shore in Weymouth.  I was in shock the whole ride.  They took x-rays( which I have) and saw the two broken bones (spiral fractures)
in my leg.  [REDACTED] did surgery and put in a rod and two pins.  I stayed there after for four days.  Then after that I went to a rehab for almost 2 months. There I did physical therapy 2 hours a day 6 days a week. I went through excruciating pain through this ordeal I'm happy to say Im home now and for you to know the skecher shapeups might look cool yet they are very dangerous and I would definately take them off the market, my opinion.  Thanks!
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, specifically a broken tibia and fibula, requiring surgery and extensive rehabilitation. The likelihood of such an incident occurring is unlikely, as it was a one-time accident involving a specific circumstance.

month-old daughter. I put the snowsuit on my daughter for the first time yesterday (11/28112). Once outside she

In early August, 2011, I wore an new Warner's bra made of elastane and nylon (model #4018). I developed deep lesions and welts on my both sides of my body where the bra pressed against my skin. I contacted Warner's who asked that I send photos and my bra, which I did. They kept the bra for 4 1/2 months, claiming they were having it examined and would send me a report of their findings. 

Warner's did no testing of the material whatsoever. Nevertheless, they stated: '"There are no toxic chemicals present in the product." They could not possibly know this simply by looking at it. Why would it take 4 1/2 months to look at a bra? (I asked them to return it, all the while mistakenly thinking they actually checked it for particular suspected chemical contaminants.)

Eventually they sent me 2 bras which I did not request and did not want. I wrote a letter to the company. The head of the Risk Management department replied, telling me that I should use the bras they sent and implied that if I washed them first I would have a different result. I laundered one of the bras along with my other laundry and wore it. At the end of the day when I was getting ready for bed I was shocked (once again) to see that the skin underneath the sides of the bra had deep lesions. I saw my family doctor and she said I had developed dermatitis. The 2d bra was also made of elastane and nylon, model #2085. 

Manufacturers should not be allowed to sell intimate apparel which causes injuries to a person's body. And if they do, they should own up to it and make it right, not send them more more toxic clothing to cause a second injury.
justification: The incident resulted in deep lesions and welts on both sides of the body, indicating an injury. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it was a specific reaction to a particular product.

After x-rays the results were a knee effusion they put me on some pain medicine, steroids and a knee immobilizer. I was to follow up with my primary care doctor and possibly  get an MRI. incident_description:
I am writing you to notify you of a potential safety hazard issue with one of Old Navy's products. I purchased the Pink Shag Swim Shoes for Baby in size 6 at their store in the Oxmoor Center in Louisville, KY on May 6, 2012. (See attached email store receipt and online product description.) I got them for my 23 month old daughter to wear to the beach and pool side not only to protect her feet from sharp objects, but to help prevent slips and falls pool side and in the pool locker room. They were a little hard to get on, but they fit her feet perfectly, so ill fit is not a factor in the danger these shoes pose in our case.

While she was wearing them on hardwood floors of our rental house while we were away on vacation at the beach, she slipped and fell several times, once really hard on her face due to these shoes. This all happened during one wearing and within a short time period of about 15 minutes or less. When she fell on her face we immediately took them off in fear of her seriously injuring herself. I did not allow her to wear them any more during our vacation and planned on returning them when we got home.ÃÂ 

Once we got home, I decided to test them pool side to see if maybe they did better on a tile surface, which is a common surface around pools and a reason that people would buy swim shoes for traction (which is what this item claims to provide in the product description). It was like she was skating on ice! Fortunately, I had anticipated this, and was holding her hand to help prevent injury due to another fall.ÃÂ 

I would like to add that I have bought several pairs of shoes from Old Navy for both of my daughters over the last 4 years, and this is not the first time I have had a safety issue with their shoes. I have purchased several other pairs of infant/toddler casual and dress shoes that all have a felt-like material on the soles, which cause loss of traction when worn on hard surface flooring such as hardwood and tile. Why would they put felt on the bottom of a toddler's shoe, let alone any shoes?! ÃÂ None of these shoes posed a risk as severe as the water shoes, and fortunately, neither of my daughters has seriously injured themselves due to any of their falls from the aforementioned shoes.

After my experience with the felt-soled shoes I had decided to never buy Old Navy infant/toddler shoes again, but I thought the water shoes would be different since the soles seemed to have grip when they are dry. I understand that water causes surfaces to be slippery, but that is why people buy water shoes/aqua socks! I, personally, and other members of my family, including my children, have had several different brands of water shoes and have never experienced slipping like this. I was even wearing mine on the same surfaces at the same time as my daughter and didn't have any problem with slipping.

After further consideration, I decided that just returning the shoes for a refund would not be the right thing to do. While it would solve my problem, it leaves many other children getting ready to hit the beach and the pool this summer vulnerable to serious injury, and possibly even death. As a result, I have decided to notify you and Old Navy of this product safety issue.  I requested that Old Navy not only issue me a full refund, but I also requested and urged them to take this product off their shelves and web site, as well as issue a voluntary recall.
justification: The incident involved a child slipping and falling multiple times while wearing the shoes, but no serious injury occurred. The shoes' design, with felt-like material on the soles, appears to be the root cause of the slipping issue.

I felt my body was getting worse so I threw them in the dumpster at work.  I bought a regular pair of skechers  and have been wearing the flat regular shoes since.  I still have back, neck, and hip issues and feel older than I actually am. I have gained weight (6 pounds)  even though I take between 13,000 and 19,000 steps a day at work.   I am only 45 years old.  I have told my Chiropractor many times "I am too young to be this old!"   My body feels it has aged tremendously and I have also told him I can't imagine getting old.  It scares me if I feel this bad now.     I have given my testimony to others who I see wearing Shape Ups hoping they will heed my warnings.     I have an account on the Skechers website that has an order history of all of my purchases.  I bought 3 pair within 1 year before I realized they were doing more damage than good.

incident_description: I was first drawn to SketchersÃÂ "Shape-Ups" ladies exercise shoes mid-year 2009 via multiple TV advertisements. These ads featured women walking, running and exercising wearing these shoes with "stated" results of losing weight, toning calf muscles and generally improving a person's physical health. Consequently, I purchased one pair in December, 2009 and wore them each day, 4 to 5 days a week, walking at least 3 miles each day. While I imagined some benefits from wearing these exercise shoes, I also began to "suddenly" lose my balance during regular workdays...wearing regular, average height, high heel shoes. This didn't occur every day...and on no occasion did my "falls" result in broken bones, but, the knowledge of some weakness in my legs and ankles became more and more pronounced so that I wore "flat" shoes often. Unfortunately I didn't initially associate my issue of periodic "imbalance" and a low-grade constant aching feeling in my legs with the use of these shoes. And even more unfortunate for me was the fact that after that first full year I was shopping one afternoon an found that a store had "shape-Ups" on sale...so I brought another pair and proceeded to wear my new shape-ups through most of 2011. Currently, I have been to several specialist regarding the now constant "pain" in both my legs (not the knees) just the lower leg muscles. However, the doctors can't find any evidence of diseased or neurological disorders. Yet, my mobility is severely compromised; I cannot sit for more than 20 to 30 minutes without having to hold on to something stable in order to get up. I can hardly sleep at night given the constant aching pain, can't wear any type of "dress" shoe with a high heel and I can't ascend or descend stairs at all. It was only a few months ago that a friend of mine (knowing of my mysterious leg ailments) asked me if were still walking everyday and wearing the "shape-Ups" I had previously raved about. When I told her noÃÂ that I was not walking everyday anymore and therefore was no longer wearing the shoes, she told me about the "Shape-ups" recall and all of the consumersÃÂ who have been in some way injured as a result of wearing the shoes. I simply would like to add my story in hopes that the company  eventually understands  how "badly" this product has impacted its intended audience and takes steps to try and "right" the wrong!
justification: The user experienced leg pain, imbalance, and mobility issues after wearing the shoes, indicating an injury. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as the user was a individual case and no widespread harm was mentioned.

incident_description: I had recieved a pair of shape-ups from my grandma as a present for my birthday, because I really wanted a pair to try and help me get into shape. I wore my shape-ups like every single day for anything I had to do. One day in April 2011 I was playing with my daughter at the park, I was wearing my shape-ups, and I ended up falling due to my leg twisting and I had a sharp pain in my leg and knee. I thought I just pulled a muscle. I went to my dr a couple days later due to my knee swelling up and bruising, and his first thought was that I had a meniscus tear in my knee, and told me to stop wearing the shape-ups that I always wore. He ordered a x-ray, and that didn't show anything wrong. So then he ordered physical therapy, and a CT Scan and MRI. After we had gotten the results back, he ordered me to see a orthropdaedic specialist because as my family dr he was unable to figure out what was wrong. So I scheduled to see a specialist. I was unable to get a appointment with him until August 2011. So for roughly 2 months I wore several different types of knee braces to try and help the pain. The  entire time I waited to see the specialist I was in severe pain and kept seeing my normal dr due to the pain I was having. Finally I seen him and he asked what had happened and had me move my leg and knee certain ways, and documented the pain and reactions I would have to the certain exercises he had me do. He told me that what I had going on, that he could see from my MRI that I had done, that I had a patellofemoral disorder, and patellofemoral instability with pain and pain syndrome. He said the only way to get rid of the problem would be to perform a arthoscopic latteral release on my knee. He said that it wasn't a guarantee that it would fix my problem, but due to the amount of time that has gone on since the date of the injury, he believes this would be the only option left. So we scheduled my surgery for September 20, 2011, and that is when I had my surgery. I never linked my knee problem to my shoes, until my friend told me there was a lawsuit against the shape ups. I decided to look into it and realized that there were things that stuck out to me, such as one woman saying she had a meniscus tear due to the shoes, and then I checked into it because I in fact was wearing my shoes when my injury occurred. While talking to my husband after reading all this online, he reminded me that in fact months ago he thought it had been because of my shoes that I had this knee injury, because he had heard that they are not good for you, and also reminded me that the dr had recommended not to wear those shoes.  And Im not overweight or play any sports, so I really shouldn't have a injury to this degree just by playing with my daughter at the park.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury requiring surgery, classified as a patellofemoral disorder and patellofemoral instability with pain and pain syndrome. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given the reported issues with the shoes and the doctor's recommendation to stop wearing them.

incident_description: My report is regarding the ThudGuard infant safety helmet. It is designed so that it straps under the child's neck. There were 2 occasions where my 17 month old daughter was wearing the helmet with it strapped as illustrated on the website and in trying to remove the helmet she pushed it off the back of her head. The helmet was hanging by the strap around her throat making her audibly choke the first time and the next time I found her laying in the floor starting to turn blue. She didn't lose consciousness and didn't stop breathing but I am afraid of what would have happened if I hadn't found her and quickly removed the helmet. Since then I have experimented with ways to use the helmet on her head without it posing a strangulation hazard but if you loosen the strap it becomes easier for her to push it off backwards and any tighter it chokes her that way. It is not designed so that it can be strapped behind her neck and you cannot remove the strap to use the helmet without it. This product is not safe in my opinion and would return the product to the company but the packaging and "invoice" (it only had a sticker label with the product name and my shipping address enclosed) got thrown away. It also did not come with any instructions or information regarding proper use of the item. I have not contacted the company and I purchased the helmet through a third party vendor (babyhaven.com) but will if I need to. I ordered the helmet around February 22nd 2012 or so and the first incident occurred within the first week of having the product.
justification: The infant experienced audible choking and turned blue, indicating a near-life threatening injury, but did not lose consciousness or stop breathing. The design flaw in the helmet poses a risk of strangulation, but the incidents described were not fatal.

incident_description: I recently purchased a brand new, in the box, pair of The Couture Collection Pediped Roman sandals from Ebay.  My granddaughter wore them for the first time on 3/16/12.  We always remove her shoes when she naps, but leave her socks on.  On the morning of 3/17/12, she layed down for her morning nap.  Thankfully I was in the room when she awoke, but she continued to play in her bed for a few minutes.  I heard her cough and then it was apparent she was  choking.  I ran and picked her up, immediately put my finger in her mouth and pulled out a clear label from her mouth in the back of her throat.  It was apparent it was a label from a shoe, but I could not immediately identify which shoe.  I also found another label of the same type, but with different writing, rolled up and stuck to the mattress protector in her bed.  I looked at all her shoes and could not find any labels to match the ones I found.  I looked at the pediped boxes to see if there were any warnings or notices of the labels and found none.  After examining several pairs of her pedipeds, I found the same exact label still attached inside the heel portion of the left Couture Collection Pediped Roman sandal.  It appears the label probably "rolled" down when she was wearing the shoe and stuck to her socks, without being noticed, when she wore the shoes on 3/16/12 and then came off the sock and stuck to something in her bed.  I did not find a label similar to the second one that was stuck to the mattress cover anywhere on the left shoe; therefore, we are diligently searching to make sure it is not in her bed somewhere.  The  box the shoes came in is a hard gold colored box, with a clear front and a paper showing different colored roman sandals.  There is a tag on the side of the box that reads:  870-SV X-Small, Aurelia Silver, 0-6 months.  There is a bar code with number:  8 45149 00622 9.  One tag that came off (the one in her mouth reads) Designed in USA, Made in China, 0-6 months/US2.5-3.5/EU17-18, Patent Pending. TLC, All leather upper, lining and sole.  The tag I found rolled up shows a drawing of three shoes, with arrows pointing to the top, inside and sole of the shoe (indicating the all leather).

This was the first that I had heard that there was a problem with this type shoe, though I had purchased a pair myself and did not like them, because I noticed a tendency of instability when I walked across a driveway sloping downward. Upon reaching the ER of the Cottonwood Hospital, the orthopedic surgeon [REDACTED] also commented about the many incidents he had seen that were related to the wearing of this shoe, and said they were dangerous. The operating room was scheduled, so he put a cast on her foot, and scheduled surgery for Monday, March 12. Following surgery, her foot again was put in a cast, with a follow-up scheduled for March 27. Her intense pain initially was to be controlled by Hydro-Codone, which was not successful, so prescription was changed to Percocet, which has been controlling her pain.

I was prescribed [REDACTED] and then [REDACTED], which caused me severe heart burn, which I treated with [REDACTED]. The x-rays seemed to be normal. My knee pain got progressively worse. Oddly enough, it is worst when I am sitting at my desk.  

Today, I saw an Orthopedic doctor, because the pain has become unbearable. He did an x-ray of my right knee and he said, in layman's terms,  both my knee caps are wearing out. I am developing arthritis. He gave me a cortisone shot in my right knee and I need PT. He told me to stop wearing the Sketchers immediately. In three weeks, I have a second visit to treat my left knee. 

Apparently, when you walk or exercise, your knees are lubricated and when at rest, they dry out. My knees pop constantly, they throb and ache deeply and after sitting for an extended time, I can barely walk when I get up.

I have two pairs of Sketchers Shape Ups. When I bought them, I was amazed at how comfortable they were. I never had chronic, debilitating knee pain in my life. I believe these sneakers are dangerous and should not be on the market. I don't know what the future holds for me.

I bought one pair at Kohls and the second in Las Vegas in May 2011, at their brand new factory store. There was no DVD to view. 

I would like to know if my problem warrants further investigation. I would like to protect others from the pain and suffering I am living with today due to these sneakers.
