incident_description:
I bought a pair of Earth Spirit Gelron 2000 shoes at Wal-mart.  The tag said they were leather and they looked quite comfortable so I paid $20 + tax for a pair of what I thought were good quality flip-flops.

The first time I wore them, after a half hour the tops of both feet were red and itchy where the center piece sat atop my foot, resembling the shape of a triangle.  It took almost 2 weeks for the redness and itching to subside, and the skin still looked dry and rough.  So I thought perhaps there was some chemical residue left from manufacturing or something, and I cleaned the lining with some peroxide and dried it off.  Turns out the lining was vinyl, not leather, and the triangle section contained the black ink stamp with brand and content information.  

Yesterday, after I wore the shoes just 4 hours, I had to return home and take them off.  My skin was beet red and looked like a 3rd degree sunburn with raised blisters full of clear liquid.  The itching was extremely intense, as well as the pain as I could not bear to touch them.  I put on solarcaine aloe gel every 2 hours to try to numb the skin.  I was unable to wear any shoe as they all involved touching the arch of my feet.  I have had vinyl-lined shoes throughout my life without ever having any experience such as this.  I cannot imagine what type of chemical can inflict this damage and I do not have the money to research the cause.  I only know that I am not the first one, after looking online I see there are many such incidents going on for 6 years already.  It is not an anomaly and I believe the manufacturer and Wal-mart should be held responsible for my pain and suffering.  My once-beautiful feet are now scarred for life, and I may wind up with cancer as a result--who knows?
justification: The incident resulted in a severe skin reaction with redness, itching, raised blisters, and pain, indicating a significant injury. The fact that similar incidents have been reported online for 6 years suggests that the occurrence of such reactions is likely.

That was October 7, 2011 at a friend's house. I went to the ER with a follow-up with my primary care physician. After over four weeks, my foot was not better and I saw a podiatrist who put me in a boot. I wore that for over six weeks, but still have considerable pain. 

The second fall was shortly after Thanksgiving and did not result in an injury. 

The third fall occurred on February 16, 2012, on stairs resulting in a badly sprained left foot and an extremely painful tailbone injury. The only time I am not in terrible pain is when I am standing; however, the act of rising is excruciating. Simple activities such as lowering myself into a seated position, sitting, rising from sitting, lying down, and going to the bathroom are painful. 
As there is only space for one date, I am filling out the form for the last incident. I am; however, going to complete this for each accident I've had. 

The three accidents were due to my foot rolling the the side rather than the heel to toe motion. At first it didn't occur to me that the shoe could be the problem until after the third accident. The only common denominator in each accident was that shoe. I also wear boots with stacked heels, regular tennis shoes, high heel shoes, and pumps and have never fallen while wearing any of these shoes. I've walked on all different kinds of surfaces including, cement, cobblestones, wet ground, uneven ground and gone up and down stairs while wearing these other types of shoes without incident. 

****I have x-rays from the Memorial Health University Medical Center and Southcoast Medical Center, both of which are located in Savannah, Georgia. I have prescriptions for pain medication from both locations. Currently I am in a lot of pain due to the two falls (October 2011 and February 2012). I didn't figure out it was the luggage til the next morning. When I arrived at home, I put the bags in my guest room open, hoping they'd air out in a day or two. That night, the same thing happened in my bedroom, I could not breathe.  I finally realized that my pajamas had been in the suitcase and now had absorbed this chemical. Once I threw them in the laundry the problem was solved. 

I had opened the box the cases came in, in my mother's bedroom and she complained all day about her allergies. I didn't pay much attention until this all happened to me. I now connect her exposure from the protective wrapping for the cases that I threw in her trash can.

 I don't know what chemical is being used either in the fabric, the plastic or the glue but it almost killed me and could have done worse to my 80 year old mother.

incident_description:
I am a 52 year old female.  I own two pairs of Sketcher Shape Ups.  
 
In May, 2010 I had severe pain in my groin, could barely walk and went to an Orthopedic and had an x-ray.  I was diagnosed with a fractured pelvis on my left side. No known cause for the injury. I had a bone density test and had my calcium levels checked and both were fine.  I had worn Shape Ups prior to the diagnosis.  
 
In February, 2011, I had severe groin pain again and went to an Orthopedic and had an x-ray.  I was diagnosed with a fracture of the pelvis (right side).  No known cause.  In March, 2011, I had a Nuclear Bone scan and a bilateral MRI of the pelvis.  When I saw my doctor for the results on 4.4.2011, the only discovery was another fracture on the right side.  No cancer or bone disease.  And again, no known cause for the injury.  Unknowingly, I had worn the shoes prior to the injuries.  That makes 3 pelvic fractures so far.  
 
I am aware of the danger of these shoes and will never wear them again. I have not worn the Skecher Shape Ups since the last fracture and I have not had any further fractures.  
 
Respectfully,
[REDACTED]
justification: The incident involved multiple injuries (pelvic fractures) to the same person, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is classified as 3 (possible) as there were repeated instances of injury but no clear causal link established.

incident_description:
My 19-yr old daughter has been wearing Reebok's RunTone shoes since December of last year.   She has been experiencing severe leg, knee and lower back pain.   She has been diagnosed as having inflamed hamstring muscles, tendonitis of the knee and has developed "Pes Anserinus bursitis" which is causing her excrutiating pain.   Her doctors and I have been at a loss as to why this would happen to a healthy, slim 19-yr old.    Her sciatic nerve has been affected also which leads to pain down both legs to her feet.

After hearing about the FTC recall of these shoes and reports of similar incidents,  I decided to file an official complaint because I want to make sure these incidents are fully investigated.  This is not just a case of false advertisement.   This is a case of a product that causes damage and severe injuries.  And it must be stopped.

This has been so bad that I started looking for Muscular Dystrophy specialists who could test my daughter because I thought this could be a form of MD or MS.  You have no idea of the worry and the pain this has caused us.   Please investigate this situation and advise users of the possible consequences of wearing Easy Tone/Run Tone shoes.
justification: The incident description reports severe leg, knee, and lower back pain, along with specific diagnosed injuries such as inflamed hamstring muscles, tendonitis of the knee, and Pes Anserinus bursitis. The multiple reported cases and the severity of the injuries suggest a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:

Some of the bodysuits have embroidered designs with a backing material on the inside to keep the embroidery thread from chafing. I didn't realize this, and when I dressed my daughter in her sleeper earlier this week the backing material had come off entirely and must have attached itself to her sleeper (static cling from the dryer).  

I didn't notice this had happened until I went to check on her at 1:00 a.m. when I found the piece of backing material IN HER MOUTH.  

Luckily she didn't try to swallow it.  This was a about a 2" x 3" piece of material - definitely a choking hazard.

They need to figure out a way to make the material adhere better to the bodysuits so this doesn't happen.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard, but no injury occurred as the child did not swallow the material. The likelihood of this specific event happening again is unlikely, given that it's a one-time occurrence with a specific product.

incident_description:
On 12/14/10 I bought my wife a pair of Reebok EASYTONER shoes which I gave her for Christmas. After a week of use of these EASYTONER shoes she experienced pain in both ankles more noticeably her right ankle and it became increasingly more difficult to use the EASYTONER shoes for any length of time.
On 1/12/11 she went to a foot doctor who administered her ankle a cortisone shot to address the pain. This shot had a very limited affect. ($135). We are on a fixed income and she has no medical coverage so we need to exercise restraint in encountering medical expenses. 

She had to limit her use of the EASYTONER shoes but the pain in the right ankle became increasingly worse so on 5/23/11 she went back to the foot doctor. He took x-rays of her right ankle. From these x-rays the ankle appeared to have experienced a hairline stress fracture. He fitted her with a cast boot ($405). The boot limited the movement of her ankle and brought some relief. Several weeks later the boot was removed and the pain again began to increase. She stopped using the EASYTONER shoes.

At the end of June, because of the continuing pain, she had to return to the foot doctor. More x-rays were taken and she was given a shoe insert for a regular shoe. (not billed yet) The insert only made the pain worse.

On 7/11/11 she went to her regular doctor. He diagnosed that she had experienced the onset of gout in the right ankle injury which occurred around the end of December and which was shortly after she began using the EASYTONER shoes. Her mother had gout so apparently my wife had a propensity for gout developing in a fracture. She was given pain medication and medication to address the gout. (lab $277; doctor not yet billed). This condition and the pain is expected to be with her for quite some timed. She now has to use a walker to ease the pain enough to get around.

It wasn't until this Reebok case became public that all the pieces came together chronologically to see the impact of the EASYTONER shoes and the subsequent injury.
justification: The incident resulted in a hairline stress fracture, gout, and ongoing pain, requiring multiple medical interventions. The severity is level 3 due to the injury, and the likelihood is unlikely (2) as there's no indication of a widespread issue with the product.

I was wearing skechers shapeup's (jumpstart) when this happened and i know without a doubt that these shoes caused this injury.   I had turned my ankle a couple times prior to this.  At one point i thought the shoes might be causing me to get off-balance, but then i thought these are tennis shoes that promote good health so that can't be it- i'll just be more careful.
I now wish i had listened to first instinct and stopped wearing the shoes.  These shoes are dangerous and I can't believe there now marketing them for children.

incident_description:
I bought these shoes on April 4 at The Walking Company in Minnetonka, MN.  I have been a fitness walker for years, walking four miles a day at least every other day.  On days I can't walk four miles I walk two miles in walking shoes and have had no problem. 

In June, the inside of my left knee started to ache and I chalked it up to getting older.  I am 54 so thought this was middle aged aches and pains.  Last Monday while I work I felt sharp jolts of pain and went to the Urgent Care doctor where I was diagnosed with an inflamed ligament, which I am to ice, wear a knee sleeve and take two Advil capsules twice a day.  The next morning, my husband read the article in the August, 2011 Consumer Reports about these shoes and it clicked.  I have had no other changes in my routine except buying these shoes.  

I didn't like the feel of them that much, but for $134 I thought I would wear them until my 500 miles were up to buy a new pair.  Now I wish I would have stopped wearing these earlier.

Finally I started feeling better and continued onto my usual routine at the gym, my 7days a week. Then not even a month or so after that injury, I ended up getting knee pain really bad. It was to the point where I couldn't walk without a limp, and took over-the-counter medications for the pain and discomfort I was having. I also places a knee brace on it thinking it would go away faster by holding it in place. But continuing on at the gym was only making the problem worse, so I had stopped going to the gym completlely, at the same time still paying my monthy expense for my membership cause I didn't want to cancel and get chatged a bunch of fees. Since then I have not used my shape-up shoes, even around at the park I haven't used them. Even after all the rest I have has since then injury, to this day I still have pain. I have days where the pain is so bad I probably take all together in one day a handful of OTC pain killers. Given the fact they don't work for the pain, I  continue to take more, and rest a lot more than usual. My life has changed a lot since the injury. I no longer can dance like I love to, exercise at the gym for the days and hours I would normally, and also can't even stand in one place too long without having to put my weight onto my right leg to prevent my left leg with the injury more pain. I am also going to school for criminal justice to be a police officer, and am praying this knee injury due to the Shape-Ups aren't going to cause any problems for me to pursue my dream.

incident_description:
April 11, 2011 had on Daskins Now athletic shoes (their version of [REDACTED]).  Gonig down deck steps to work in the morning.  Around the second or third step, went to place my left leg on the step and the next think I knew there was great pains in my legs as I smacked the ground. Two hospital stays for infection, two surgeries.  On the second time seeing primary care doctor regarding my legs from the fall, he sent me to emergency for evaluation and admittance; was admitted and given high quantities of antibiotics intravenously; number of doctors came in to evaluate my thigh; plastic/reconstructive surgeon removed a lot of old blood via needles then debrided area leaving a large open wound that went down to my muscle.  This hospital stay was in May, 2011.  Second infection developed around the end of May, 2011 (around Memorial Day weekend).  Saw the plastic surgeon at the end of that week, on Friday; he had me admitted into the hospital for more antibiotics intravenously and did surgery the next day (Saturday).  An incision in my leg below my knee was made and the inside of the leg was cleaned between my large open wound adn the new incision.  The new incision was also to help drain the large wound.  Was off work from end of May to about end of July, 2011.

These shoes are a danger to anyone who wears them and should be taken off the market!

incident_description:
I bought some Keen River sandals for hiking.  They were defective.  The seams that hold the ankle together failed after 15 days of use.  The seams that hold the shoe to the ankle failed in three different places on the same day - two places on the left sandal and one on the right sandal.  

They began to fall apart when I was on a steep trail far from camp.  I had to scramble over rocks and cross ledges to get back to camp.  If the shoes failed at a critical point along the trail, they could have caused a serious fall that could have resulted in injury or death.  Even if they did not cause injury, if they failed far from camp, I would have been stranded - the trail was too rugged to traverse without footwear.  

I will attach photographs of the failure points.  The photos show that one ankle seam has almost completely detached.  Two photos show loose silver threads that are still attached at both ends. These seam threads are intact, they did not fail from abrasion.  Rather they failed because the stitches were not properly anchored in the material of the shoe. My guess is the bobbin ran out of thread and Keen's quality control did not notice the problem. The neoprene of the support would have held the threads for a few days until the stress of use pulled them loose.  

The photos show that the same type of failure occurred at three different locations on the shoes- two places on the left sandal and one on the right
I reported this to Keen and they said they had never heard of the problem, but there are several reviews on Amazon.com that complain about this exact problem.
Keen should recall these shoes and reinforce the ankles.
justification: The incident involved defective shoes that could have led to a serious fall and potentially caused injury or death if they failed at a critical point, but fortunately, no injury occurred. The likelihood of occurrence appears possible given multiple reports of similar issues with the same type of shoe.

incident_description:
I am filing this report in the hopes it will save others from the injury I incurred while wearing Skecher Shape-ups sneakers.  

On July 17, 2011, I was walking with my husband in a local park.  I was wearing Sketcher Shape-ups sneakers and have worn them many times before.  We were walking a study pace as I approached a slight ramp from the street to the sidewalk.  As I stepped onto the ramp, my sneakers literally rocked me forward causing me to loose my balance and I landed flat on my face.  Upon falling, I slammed the sidewalk with my teeth and nose.  I have never tripped while walking before and went down so fast that I had no time to break my fall. My body lunged forward and I landed directly on my face.  I hit so hard and there was so much blood that I thought for sure I had lost my teeth and broken my nose.  The impact to my previously perfect straight teeth has caused them to shift, my nose now has a slight and probably permanent bump and I have a scar on my lip.  Unfortunately, it is still possible to develop an absess in my gums adversely effecting my teeth, so I will not know the permanent damage to my teeth for 6 months to a year.  My teeth are still sensitive to hot and cold four weeks after this incident, my nose is still very tender and I no longer have perfectly straight teeth.  However, at this time I still have my teeth and am thankful for that.  When this accident happened, my husband took me to the local emergency center in town, I have also visited the dentist 3 times for pain and shifting of my teeth as well as to a doctor for evaluation of damage to my nose.  

In my opinion, the shape-ups should be taken off the market.  I am by no means accident prone, I feel the design of these sneakers can cause great damage to anyone.  I would rather be less tone and have my teeth.  After all, the health of your body is effected by the over all health of your teeth.

incident_description:
After spending months exercising by walking in Sketchers Shape Ups, I developed Exercise-Induced Compartment Syndrome in both lower legs. 

I was walking 3 to 5 miles a day in these shoes. Because of the rocker soles, the shoes force the wearer to pull up on the toes more, which results in over-developed muscles (specifically Tibialis Anterior) which then push up against the fascia during exercise causing extreme pressure and pain and loss of muscle control.

After a few months, the symptoms started. I was unable to walk a mile before I had to stop to alleviate the pressure and pain.  It finally got to the point where I could not walk a couple blocks before the pain and pressure started. 

I ended up having to go through Physical therapy and then a very painful surgery - Bi-Lateral Fasciatomies on February 25, 2011. The surgeon had to cut the fascia surrounding the muscle compartments in both legs so that the muscles would no longer cause pressure and pain. 

At least 2 Doctors and the physical therapist stated that this condition was caused by these shoes. Compartment Syndrome does not occur in walkers - mostly runners and a few other sports, but not walking. But because of the way these shoes force the foot, ankle, and lower leg to be used in different ways, this injury occurred.

I started exercising in these shoes in June of 2010 and the surgery was February 25, 2011.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury, Exercise-Induced Compartment Syndrome, requiring physical therapy and surgery. The likelihood of occurrence is considered unlikely as it is an unusual condition not commonly associated with walking.

I am now scheduled for surgery on September 12, 2011 and will need to miss work for this procedure.
justification: The incident resulted in a torn meniscus, causing significant pain and impacting the person's lifestyle, which corresponds to a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of this specific occurrence is unlikely, as it was triggered by a specific and sudden event (twisting and placing minimal weight on the leg).

incident_description: I purchased a pair of Sketcher's Shape up sneakers to tone my legs and buttocks. I am a nurse and spend a lot of time on my feet, and thought I could put that time to good use. After wearing them for approximately three months I noticed some tenderness and pain in my left instep, arch, heel and bottom of my left foot when I took them off. I did not fall or turn over on my ankle while wearing them. It was a gradual injury over time. I had to go to my doctor because I could no longer stand the pain in my foot and ankle. After an x-ray and MRI of my ankle it was determined that I had torn ligaments and tendonitis in my left foot and ankle. I cannot explain the excrutiating pain that I experience in my ankle, especially at night while trying to sleep. I have lost countless hours of sleep, plus I must wear an ankle brace both during the day to be able to walk and one at night in able to sleep. I am taking pain medication round the clock. Ultimately I will need surgery to correct the damage that was done to my foot and ankle.These people need to be held accountable for this damage. I know that I am not the only person in this situation. Not only do they NOT tone muscles, they injure them instead.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, including torn ligaments and tendonitis, requiring medical treatment, pain medication, and potentially surgery. The injury was not an isolated event, as the complainant mentions others may have experienced similar issues.

incident_description: On a trip to Washington DC with my family, we balanced our sight seeing experience by bus, boat and walking.   On one of the walking days, I rolled my left ankle to a very painful extreme.  The rocker bottom and height of the Skechers Shape Ups that I was wearing caused the roll and accentuated the extent of my injury.  As a result, I ended up with a 2 1/2 cm tear in the peroneal tendon of my left ankle.  The healing process required two surgeries, 20 doctor visits, 70 days of missed work, 76 days in 6 different casts, 112 days in a brace support for walking, 900 minutes of physical therapy, 450 minutes of home therapy and 42 days of strict bed rest.  From all of this recovery, I had to check myself into [REDACTED] to help return my body to its "presketchers" shape and weight--a far cry from the shapely body they promise as a result of wearing these shoes.  Prior to this injury, I had been wearing shape ups for about three months, gradually building up a tolerance before wearing them for extended periods of time.  It is now 18 months after the first surgery and I still cant wear regular shoes--I am only able to wear flip flops or clogs due to continued swelling accompanied with pain on the left ankle.  This has greatly reduced my ability to exercise or travel by foot.  I have had to make many lifestyle adaptations including a new top load washer/drier and a heightened toilet to name just a few.  I cringe whenever I see someone wearing Skechers Shape Ups.  They have changed my life in a very adverse way.  Losing the gift of my left ankle has been the greatest handicap in my life.  Skechers Shape Ups are responsible.  The general public needs to be informed of the great risks involved with wearing these shoes.  If I could go back in time knowing what I know today, i would never have laced up in Skechers Shape Ups.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury, including a 2.5 cm tear in the peroneal tendon, requiring surgeries, extensive medical treatment, and long-term impact on the individual's lifestyle. The likelihood of such an injury occurring is unlikely, as it was caused by a specific combination of factors, including the design of the shoes and the individual's usage pattern.

He gave me some pain pills and an prescription for Naproxen as well, also advising me to ice the site.  I followed his instructions, but saw no relief. I have been advised by an sports orthopedic doctor that surgery should be considered to repair the tears.  I am very reticent to have surgery, but, I suppose it will be necessary to get me back to the ability to exercise, or to even walk without pain and limping!

incident_description:
I was shopping at a shoe outlet and after being therefor an hour touching shoes and boots my lower lip area began itching on my way home.  This then led to the lip oozing and over the next week it became dry, peeled off and eventually healed.  The following week, with my lip being better, I went to the same outlet, and the same reaction occurred.  This time, on my way home, I visited a local clinic for a physician to look at it to make sure it was not a medical condition.  He was an emergency doctor, not an allergist, and said it was some sort of reaction and prescribed antihistimines for itching.
The same process happened, the lip dried out, peeled and healed.  Yesterday, two weeks after the last incident, I was in the local mall.  I was in a Macy's and picked up a Michael Kors MK Logo Rain Boot which was on display.  I was drinking a coffee at the time as well.  I placed the coffee down, touched the boot with both hands, then picked up my coffee from the top (touching where I would drink from) and walked away.  Within 5 minutes, my lip began to itch again, and the whole process started again.  Ironically, on the visit to the shoe outlet two weeks prior, I recall picking up the same boot and the itching started within minutes.  I am not allergic to latex, as I have been allergy tested in October 2010.  After speaking to someone with a chemistry backround, they believe what I am experiencing is actually not an allergic reaction, but a chemical reaction.  These boots were most likely made from molds, which chemicals are sprayed into to avoid the boot from sticking to the mold.  I wanted to contact you with my story in case anyone else has had same incidents.  Plus, this may be dangerous for babies and children.
justification: The incident caused an injury with symptoms including itching, oozing, and peeling of the skin, but no life-threatening conditions were reported. The repeated occurrence of similar reactions under similar circumstances suggests a likely chance of occurrence.

incident_description: June 2010, I purchased cheap pair of wedge-heeled flip-flops from local Walmart store in Toledo, Ohio to wear to the pool. August 2010 I noticed nickel-size red, itchy, dry, and cracked painful spot of irritation on the sole of my right foot. I also observed two similarly painful spots on both feet, but predominantly on the right foot, where the back straps that fit into the bottom of the shoe came into contact with my feet, and a small round dry spot on the side of right foot where the flip-flop strap wrapped around my foot. August 2010, I stopped wearing the shoes. Left foot was okay after that.  However, the health and condition of right foot became progressively worse. It became hot to the touch, red, swollen heel, thickened, peeling, flaking skin, blisters, bleeding spots, color changed from healthy pink to dark blue/purplish, in addition to the symptoms already mentioned at the start. I was unable to wear a whole shoe. Ultimately, I had to wear whole shoe due to the change in weather from warmer temperatures to very cold temperatures. Pain in the foot became so unbearable that November 2010 I began to seek medical treatment. The agony and pain drove me into Toledo and Flower hospital emergency rooms where I saw medical professionals who attempted to relieve the pain, although they were not sure what was actually causing the pain. I was prescribed  antifugal and antibacterial creams and pain medication. I was told to visit my primary care physician, which I did and he began to refer me out to other medical professionals/specialists for diagnoses and testing. Over a 6 - 7 month period, I have visited  two dermatologists, an internal medical care physician, a podiatrist, a vascular care specialist, and a neurologist. I also have an appoinment to be seen by an allergist. I have been prescribed antibiotics, narcotic pain medication, nerve pain medication, clobetasol steroid cream and ointment, along with antibacterial cleansers and lubricating creams, lotions, and ointments. I am still unclear as to my exact diagnosis but the doctors have treated it as an eczema/allergic contact dermatitis. Research has shown that flip-flop sandals sold and distributed by Wal-Mart come from China. These sandals have been pre-treated with a combination of chemicals known to cause blistering burns to the feet. These caustic and toxic chemicals have been identified as Thiuram and Dithiocarbamates. I am concerned that as innocent consumers, many people who have purchased, or will purchase these sandals will have to endure the pain, suffering, medical costs, overall interruption of one's routine of life due to the injuries they have caused. The manufacturers should, out of good faith, attach a warning label on these shoes indicating that caustic chemicals, such as the ones named in this complaint, are used to manufacture and produce these shoes so that the consumer can decide for themselves if they want to deal invite the effect of these chemicals into their lives. I work for the State Public School system as a traveling Special Education Tutor, serving 3 different elementary schools, tutoring 13 students each school day. This serious foot condition has caused me much pain and suffering, medical bills, and loss of income due to a significant number of missed days of work because of not being able to walk or stand on the foot. The problem was not limited to the skin, but has resulted in several layers of skin burned with resulting nerve damage. When walking, I had to walk on my toes to avoid pressure on the bottom of my foot. I had to wear shoes without enclosed heels to avoid pressure on the my heels. Eventually, I had to resort to a surgical/diabetic shoe to have a shoe of some sort to wear. I still have the shoes and I want to report that I had none of these problems until I wore those shoes.
justification: The incident resulted in a significant injury with symptoms including painful skin irritation, blisters, bleeding spots, and nerve damage, but did not result in death. The likelihood of occurrence appears to be unlikely as it is a specific case related to a particular product.

incident_description:
I bought a pair of Skecher Tone-Ups fitness shoes in February of 2011, mainly to use while exercising and walking. I wore them sporadically for two months, mostly on the weekends while running errands and some hiking. On April 23rd, we had relatives visit us here in the Washington DC area, so we went with them on a walking tour of the capitol area, seeing the memorials, the Capitol building, and the White House. All told, we probably walked about 10 miles. I was wearing the Tone-Ups during this time. The next day (Sunday, April 24th), I noticed a sharp pain in my right foot, on the outside part near my little toe. I attributed it to a possible pulled muscle or strain, due to the amount of walking the previous day. I figured it would get better over time, so I just went about my usual routine. After about a week and a half, the pain was persistent, so I called an made an appointment with a podiatrist (this was on Monday, May 2nd, and the appointment was on Tuesday, the 3rd). On Monday afternoon, as I was walking home from work, I felt something pop in my foot, which was followed by more intense pain. The next day, the podiatrist Xrayed my foot and found that I had fractured the fifth metatarsal in my right foot. The popping sensation was caused by the complete fracture of the bone, which obviously had a stress fracture that caused the initial pain. When I told the doctor about the Tone-Ups shoes, he said that they were not good to wear, and they can cause problems, like what I experienced. 

I am an active walker, and I usually walk at least 3 miles everyday, most of which is to and from work during the week, in dress shoes. I have never experienced problems in the past like this. I am convinced that the Skechers caused the issue that led to the fracture. These shoes should be taken off of the market.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, specifically a fracture of the fifth metatarsal in the right foot, which required a doctor's visit and X-ray. The likelihood of occurrence is considered unlikely as there is no indication of similar incidents happening frequently with these shoes.

incident_description: I bought some sketcher shoes after Christmas.  I'd been wanting to try some since the commercials claim they can help you loose weight and tone up. But then people kept talking about them--how they had some, etc., so I went back and purchased them.  They are completely white.  I've been wearing them for 4 months now daily.  They are comfortable to wear, and you get use to them after wearing them for a week or so, and they don't feel funny anymore (no more rocking action).  But then the ball of my feet started hurting--burning, especially the right foot.  I didn't know why.  I wore some other shoes for a couple days, and then went back to them thinking maybe I was still getting use to them.  My daughter thought they were ugly (she's 13 years old), and commented that maybe they weren't good for me.  Then I heard a lady talking about her's being defective and causing her right foot to hurt.  At the time I heard this mine was no longer hurting, so I just thought it was part of getting use to the shoe (like the rocking motion).  I continued to wear them, and the ball of my feet seemed okay now.  But now my right knee is hurting--like I twisted it or something.  I don't know what I did to cause this.  Maybe I did something that I am unaware of.  But I started researching my knee pain on the computer, because I can't afford to go to the doctor at every ache and pain, and don't want to go to the doctor, and I determined that it was due to overpronating (walking too much to the inside of the foot).  I am currently wearing a knee brace with metal pieces on the sides to keep my knee from twisting.  I get a sharp pain under my kneecap when I twist my leg. Anyway, it says that the pain in the ball of your feet is due to your weight being distributed wrong and putting your weight on the top of your foot, which is what the shoe does with the rocking motion.  My daughter alway said I wasn't wearing them correctly, because she said I was suppose to put my heel down first and then rock to my toes.  So I tried to concentrate on doing this at times, throwing my weight on my heels first to keep pressure off the ball of my foot.  Other times I just walked normally--tired of concentrating.  Then my research said to look at your shoes for wear points and the shapes of the shoes, which can cause problems.  Both Sketchers shoes are straight on the outsides and curve inward on the insides  All my other shoes are contoured on the outside and inside and not straight like these on the outside.  It said to look for shoes without a lot of curve, and that are basicly straight to avoid foot and knee pain and overpronation.  Then I started thinking that just maybe the Sketcher shoes are bad for me like my daughter said.  I researched the Sketcher comments and saw that other people have complained of knee problems after wearing them also.  Also, I have not lost any weight, or toned anything.  Actually, I have weight gain that's puzzling me.  I've decided now to put these shoes in the closet and go back to wearing regular shoes.  Knee pain just started on 4/27/11.

incident_description:
On July 11, 2010 I bought a Lined-Heated jacket from Susquehanna Valley Harley Davidson in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. I had it on for about 10 to 15 minutes and then hung it up until March 19, 2011. That is when this all happened. My boyfriend [REDACTED], and 2 friends of ours, [REDACTED] & [REDACTED]  decided to go for a ride to Reading, Pennsylvania to watch a high school basketball game. We live in Lewisberry, Pennsylvania so it is about a 2 hour trip. It was chilly out so I decided to try my jacket out. My friend [REDACTED] said he wasn't using his thermostat for his jacket and wanted to know if i wanted to try his before I bought one. I said that I would like to try it so we hooked it up. These jackets come with a on/off switch, you can purchase a thermostat as option to control the heat. The on/off switch is heat on, heat off, no adjusting. The way you hook the thermostat up is by plugging one end into the jacket and the other end into the motorcycle battery outlet. 

We left Lewisberry and rode to Campbelltown, Pennsylvania and stopped for lunch, as we were riding I really wasn't getting any heat so I thought I either pulled the plug out by accident or possibly turned the wrong knob on the thermostat. We ate lunch and [REDACTED] hooked it back up and continued on our way to the game. On the way to the game I noticed the jacket was working but there was one spot on my back that was getting a little warmer than the rest of my upper body. We got to the game and watched it. Two hours later we were on our way home. As we rode home the jacket was getting hotter and hotter and I kept turning it down and the one spot on my back was getting sore. We got to Hershey, Pennsylvania and stopped for dinner. I told everyone that it felt like my back was burnt in this one spot. I said the jacket kept getting hot and I kept turning it down. We ate and then before we left [REDACTED] said that he would like his thermostat back so he could wear it. I went to pull the thermostat off the jacket and I couldn't. It was still warm to the touch. [REDACTED] tried to pull it apart and so did [REDACTED], nobody could get the thermostat off so we decided to go home and deal with it later. I never plugged it back into the bike because my back was sore. 

When we got home we tried to get the thermostat off again and still couldn't. I asked [REDACTED] to please look at my back because it hurt. He lifted my shirt up and said that my back was burnt. He said it was all red and had three burn marks and blisters there. We thought about going to the doctor but decided to put some antibotic creme on it and took pictures of the burns. 

Sunday, my back still hurt and [REDACTED] said that my back was worse and the three blisters on it were getting infected. He put more creme on it and we called our friends and told them that my back was burnt and that we still couldn't get the thermostat off of the jacket. We all decided that Monday after work we would take the jacket back to SVHD. 

On Monday I continued to put creme on my back, and when I got to work I called SVHD and they told me to bring the jacket in. Monday evening, myself, [REDACTED] and [REDACTED] took the jacket back to SVHD. We talked to [REDACTED], Marketing Coordinator at SVHD and showed her the jacket and pictures of my back. She tried to get the thermostat off and could not. Another employee tried to get it off and they couldn't. [REDACTED] then said that he wanted to try one more time and just like that it came apart. SVHD did give me another jacket and told [REDACTED] that they would replace his thermostat if it didn't work. [REDACTED] gave me the number to call Harley Davidson customer service. 

On Tuesday March 22, 2011, I called [REDACTED] at Harley Davidson and she took my claim over the phone. Over the next couple of weeks [REDACTED] got the jacket and supposedly had it tested. They claim that the jacket was found to be operating properly and there is no evidence of any overheating of any kind. There was however evidence of an improper fit, a creased area in the back. 

I'm sorry but an improper fit does not burn someone and leave blisters on my back and I still to this day, I have permanate scars on my back from this. No, I did not go to the doctor because I just treated it myself.

incident_description:
I became a jewelry maker in 2010, and made a purchase of toggle clasps from Fire Mountain in August 2010 through their online catalog. They were delivered by mail to my home here in VA. Just this weekend, I read a notice from another jeweler about a product recall by Pure Allure sold via Michaels, for toggle clasps produced in China, decorated with Swarovski crystals.
Although I had purchased from Fire Mountain, I still checked. And I discovered that although Fire Mountain issued a different purchasing code number, when I looked on the back of the packaging, the packaging of the toggle clasps I bought said Pure Allure, the image of a rhinestone encrusted heart dangle matched the recalled product. Those clasps were included in bracelet making kits.
Three years after the Michaels recall, and Fire Mountain is still selling the hazardous product, and not letting consumers know that it is a hazard.

Fire Mountain never mentioned a recall, never said in their description that the product contained unsafe levels of lead. They sold me a hazardous product that had been recalled 3 years ago by a different company, and never said a word to me about the hazard, although they admitted to selling me the hazardous product in the phone conversation.

About the phone call to Fire Mountain about the lead hazard:
I called Fire Mountain today 4-17-2011 and the customer service person knew nothing about the issue. I transferred to her supervisor, and asked, why was I not told there were unsafe levels of lead in the product and why is it still being sold 3 years after the recall? She said that "there's lead in everything metal unless it says lead free", and that my state "did not have a lead law to prevent them selling it to me".

She said it was "a perfectly useful product", and "the only way to get lead into the system was to chew it." I said, babies chew on parents' jewelry. She said "We advise not selling to children under 15." I said, I don't, but I have no control over what the adult purchaser does with the product. Since the clasps are a health hazard, my only recourse is to recall all items I have made using the hazardous material, and replace them with lead free toggles. This is a lot of work for me, and a lot of additional labor and expense. But I cannot market an unsafe product, now that I know it is unsafe.

I told the Fire Mountain supervisor that my bottom line is, they knowingly sold me an unsafe product, and did not warn me of its being unsafe, and that I would have to report it. So I am, in this message.

Fire Mountain says they have a 100% guaranteed return policy if you're unhappy for any reason. But when you read the fine print, it says it must be returned in the original packaging. Since I bought the product to use in my own jewelry making, and did so, it is long out of the original packaging. So I am unable to comply with their requirement.

Since it was a product subject to recall for health hazard, and since they admit knowing about the hazard 3 years after the recall, but are still selling the product, I want Fire Mountain to have to recall it, and to run a public announcement that they sold it, to warn Fire Mountain consumers.
I also want my money back. I will never get back the time and effort put into my own work, that I now have to recall, and replace.

I had also donated some jewelry making supplies to a young mother with small children, and I must now contact her and tell her to throw those toggles away, because of the lead content. I am e-mailing her next, with a copy of this report.

With concern, [redacted]
justification: The incident involved the sale of a hazardous product with unsafe levels of lead, which was recalled 3 years prior, but no injury was reported. The product was not directly linked to any injury or death, however, its potential for harm, especially to children, was noted.

incident_description:
I purchased the "Rainier" style ladies shoes by Terrasoles (www.terrasoles.com), a brand owned by the R. G. Barry Corporation in mid-September, 2010. I got them at a high-end shoe store in the Washington, DC area. The shoes are extremely comfortable, but I noticed that they seemed as though they would easily slide on a smooth, polished flooring surface, such as those found in airports & train stations. They were fine outside, and I wore them a lot before the weather turned colder.
 I put them on again yesterday for the first time since last fall. I went outside, across my wooden porch, down one (wooden) step--and on the second (painted, dry concrete) step, my right foot slid out from under me, and I fell down hard onto the concrete steps. I was not in a hurry, and these are steps I have used several times each day for the past 10 years. They were not wet, and there were no obstacles. 
 I now have a fractured/dislocated tailbone and a slightly sprained ankle, and am in extreme pain when not taking strong pain medication. I could easily have broken my back or sustained a head injury if there had been more than two steps remaining when I fell.

    The shoes have a densely felted type of sole on the bottom. It is cross-hatched, but that is useless. My husband took one of the shoes and, with his hand inside it, placed it on our hardwood floors. He was amazed at how easily it slid--it's basically the same type of material as you find on the bottom of those small furniture-moving pads, which are rubberized on the top & felted on the bottoms. 

    These shoes are an accident waiting to happen (as it did to me!), and I'm amazed the company hasn't been sued for serious injury already. If these shoes are to remain on the market, they MUST have a non-felted sole!
justification: The incident resulted in a fractured/dislocated tailbone and a sprained ankle, indicating a moderate to severe injury. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible due to the specific conditions described, but not guaranteed.

It feels like my bone is bumpy.  It was real tender to touch.  Recently, I have had tremendous pain upon getting up in the morning, and standing after sitting for any length of time. I can hardly walk at first.  My heel and tendon is really tight, and painful.  After I am up and about, and walk on it for awhile, it loosen's up, and is less painful to walk on.  I went to my podiatrist last month, and he diagnosed it as enthesopathy, and prescribed a night brace.  I wore the brace for the first few nights, and the pain wasn't there in the morning, however, I cannot sleep with the brace.  It's big, cumbersome, and makes my heel burn for the first hour or so.  VERY hard to sleep with.  I am planning on making an appointment with my primary physician, to see what he says about it.  I have since quit wearing the shoes, and really hope that this will remedy the problem.  I am hoping this injury is not permanent.

I can't say for sure if the shoes caused this, but all I know is that when I am off for 5-6 days in a row, and not wearing the shoes, my foot seems to not hurt as bad, especially when I am usually barefooted, but after working one shift, the next day, it's extremely tight and painful again.

I think the reason I have this problem with the shoes is because I walk heavy on my heels (which is why I liked them, they put no pressure on the heel), but at the same time, I think I step down on my heel hard, and it has pulled the tendon.

After speaking with another person who also had the same experience, I conclude that there is a correlation between wearing toning shoes and developing blood clot with persons especially with a history of DVT.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury (superficial blood clot), and given the user's history of DVT, there is a plausible link to the shoes. However, the likelihood of this occurrence is considered unlikely as it is based on personal experience and one other anecdotal case.

incident_description: Consumer wanted to report that she was injured using the skechers foot wear. She had purchased these shoes for work and wore them for three weeks until feeling discomffort. During this time she was under orthopedic car. She is a nurse  and is always on her feet. She went and spoke with the retailer and they had agreed to offer a refund. She has not spoken to the manufacture as of yet. She woke up one morning and couldnt put any weight on her feet. She decided to recieve medical care in March of 2010. She feels that it was imperative to convey what happened to while using this product.
justification: The consumer developed a stress fracture in her foot after using the shoes for three weeks, resulting in an injury that required medical care and a walking boot for 8 weeks. The injury was specific to the use of the product, indicating an incident with injury.

incident_description:
3-11-11 I was exercising wearing Reebok Runtone shoes. I had not worked out in these shoes at gym before, had only been walking neighborhood. Had always worn other shoes for workout. I worked out on treadmill and did other resistance exercises that I have done the past 2 years without any injuries. That evening the ball of my left foot began feeling bruised, tender and started swelling. I rested with no exercise for 4 days, but continued to attempt normal walking. The pain increased so much I could not bare weight on the left foot. The area remained swollen, more tender and bruised with a knot feeling in the middle. I went to Ortho Dr. on 3-15-11 diagnosed with possible stress fracture - Dr. stated so much trauma and swelling hard to see. Diagnosed with strained tendons & ligamentsand symptoms of stress fracture. I was put in a boot and instructed to continue taking Alieve and ice twice a day and elevate left foot as much as possible. I returned to Dr. on 3-18-11 with pain even worse (unbearable) and swelling has not subsided at all. He orderd MRI of left foot - awaiting results. Put me on Lortab for pain, instructed remain in boot, and use crutches and elevate foot. I have had to be off work 1 week because of this.
After research and talking to others, it seems the "tone" shoes cause ortho injuries and are NOT safe to wear because they  cause one to walk in a different manner in attempt to "tone". Even the commercials show people working out in these shoes. I feel these shoes are NOT safe to wear and need to removed from the market for reassessment for safety. The injuries are painful and costly.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury, as evidenced by the symptoms of a strained tendons and ligaments and possible stress fracture, and required medical attention and time off work. The likelihood of occurrence is classified as possible, given that the user had not previously experienced issues with similar exercises but the new shoes may have contributed to the injury.

incident_description: Wore toning shoe sold by Kmart for two days while vactioning in Germany, May 2010. By end of second day could not walk. incident_description:
On March 22, 2011 I went to Footlocker to purchase a new pair of shoes.  I was looking for good walking shoes as I am on my feet all day at work and do a lot of walking.  They recommended Reebok Easytone athletic shoes.  I tried them on and they felt comfortable on the bottom of my feet.  I purchased these shoes and went home.  I read the information supplied in the booklet they included in the box which explained that the toning part was an "instability cushion" located in the bottom of the shoes that would tone portions of the calf, upper thigh, and buttocks muscles.  I wore the shoes at work on 3/23 and 3/24.  At the end of my shift on 3/24 I noticed a lot of pain and swelling in the inside of my left ankle.  I did not wear the shoes again.  On 3/25 I could not put any weight on my left ankle and notified my doctor.  During my visit we xrayed my foot and nothing was broken.  I showed him the shoes I had worn and he stated that due to the constant instability caused by the "instability cushion" I had aggravated the tendon and possibly tore ligaments in my ankle.  I was given inflammatory medication and my ankle is wrapped in an ace bandage.  I am unable to work until this heals which I am told could take up to 4-6 weeks.  

I feel that these Reebok Easytone shoes are unsafe for consumers and should not be sold.  The "instability cushion" causes harm to the ankle just by walking in the shoes.  There is no mention in the booklet included with the shoes about the stress placed on the ankle.  

Please contact me if you have any questions
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the ankle, including pain, swelling, and possible ligament tears, which required medical attention and a recovery period of 4-6 weeks. The injury was caused by the 'instability cushion' in the shoes, indicating a potential risk to users.

I cracked my right ankle and then fell on my left knee which broke the inside of my left tibia.

I believe it was because of these toning shoes that I fell.  I have been walking in and out of my house for months in my regular tennis shoes with no problem so I am sure it was because of these shoes that I have sustaided these injuries.
justification: The incident resulted in injuries, specifically a cracked right ankle and a broken left tibia, indicating a severity level of 3. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as the individual had previously walked in and out of their house without issue in regular shoes.

incident_description:
I purchased a NEW pair of protective knee pads to use while working on projects around my home.  I was only able to wear a knee pad on my LEFT due to the knee pad not fitting my right leg. No one else used or touched the product.  I used the product on several occasions over a 3 day period while doing various painting, and projects working on flooring in my home.  Within 2 days after wearing the knee pad, I developed a small, pimple looking, boil on the front of my left knee.  The skin was not broken, but it appeared to look like an in-grown hair.  Within 1 day the boil became painful and reddish. Within 2 days my left knee started to swell and the boil was now very red and VERY painful and I was having trouble walking on my left leg.  After 5 days, I went to the hospital emergency room, and was admitted to Baylor Hospital in Dallas Texas for a severe Staphylococcus infection in my knee. For a full week in the hospital, I had to be treated with antibiotics through I.V. and required surgery on my knee to remove the infected tissue. After release from the hospital, I am required to continue the daily I.V Antibiotic treatment for 1 month.    

I am almost positive that the bacteria that caused the infection came directly from my contact with this knee pad. The product is Trufit Knee Pads, Distributed by BD Medical, Franklin Lakes NJ, 07417  The product package indicates they are manufactured in China.   I still have the product in its original package, sealed in a zip lock bag.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe Staphylococcus infection requiring hospitalization, surgery, and prolonged antibiotic treatment, which corresponds to an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely (2) as the infection appears to be an isolated incident related to a specific product.

incident_description: I received a pair of Skechers Shape-ups as a gift and began to wear them according to instructions.  Within two weeks I have developed severe debilitating knee and hip pain and I believe it is due to these shoes.  At first, they felt good - like they were helping to align my posture.  I didn't really feel any of the purported "work out" benefit, but they seemed comfortable and I continued to increase the amount of time I was walking in them.  Now I have excruciating bilateral knee pain and need to have an MRI on both legs to determine the source of injury.  I can barely walk.  I also started having hip pain - deep joint pain that made me nauseous it was so intense.  Since I stopped wearing the shoes, the hip pain has subsided, but the knee pain continues and is beyond anything I have ever experienced in intensity.  I am seriously concerned that I have permanently injured my knees.  I'm not sure if the shoes change your alignment somehow or exactly where the problem is.  One thing I experienced is that is nearly impossible to turn your foot on certain surfaces causing one to wrench the knee to the side, but they also change your gait.  Nothing else in my life has changed - I have tried no other new shoes, no change in work or recreational habits, no falls or stumbles....these shoes are the only thing that can be causing this.  I wish I could say that my knee pain improved after I stopped wearing them, but so far it has not.  It is intense enough that 800 mg of ibuprofen is not putting a dent in it.  I feel  I should have researched these more thoroughly before trying these shoes, but I guess I assumed they would be good for me.  It never occurred to me that a shoe could cause this sort of injury.  I don't think anyone should be wearing them and if they do try them, they should be made aware of potential injury and warned to discontinue use at the first sign of discomfort.  I wish I had know.
justification: The incident resulted in severe debilitating knee and hip pain, requiring medical evaluation, which aligns with a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is classified as 3 (possible) as the complainant's experience is a personal anecdote, not a widespread reported issue.

incident_description:
The consumer contracted an infection from contact dermatitis due to the toxic dyes in the shoes.  The consumer went through multiple toe amputations, a lower leg amputation and then died of sepsis as a result of the infection on February 5, 2023.

ADDENDUM:  per attached letter from submitter/attorney
July 16, 2024


VIA EMAIL: clearinghouse@cpsc.gov US Consumer Product Safety Commission ATTN: Reports
4330 East-West Highway
Bethesda, MD 20814

Re:	Clarks Americas Recall 23-036 Notification of injury and death

To Whom It May Concern:

We are a bit confused by the refusal to post our notification of claim but hopefully this letter will resolve all issues.

Benzidine is a well-established carcinogen and most of the scientific and medical journal research in the last couple of decades has focused on its carcinogenic properties, but as early as the 19_, peer reviewed journal articles determined that benzidine caused increase rates of contact dermatitis in factory workers who were working with benzidine dyes. These journal articles established that contact dermatitis is seen in a statistically significant number of persons (such as factory workers) who are repetitively exposed to the dyes, without personal protection over the skin. [REDACTED] wore the Clarks shoes that were laden with benzidine dyes without socks on her foot and wore these slip-on shoes for a number of weeks prior to developing her contact dermatitis. It is well established that persons suffering contact dermatitis can develop infection on the affected area. [REDACTED] medical records indicated that she suffered the first infection on a topical superficial area of her right toes, where she developed an outbreak, which later became septic and she died as a result of this original infection.

All of her medical records were provided to [REDACTED], an endocrinologist with over 30 years experience in treating patients with diabetic ulcers as well as other afflictions. His comprehensive report is attached with his conclusions that this was a contact dermatitis which became infected and then septic.

Although not attached to this submission, we have consulted with both a internal medicine doctor with a toxicology degree, as well as with a wound care specialist and both of these specialists have concluded that this was a contact dermatitis irritation/infection caused by benzidine dye exposure and irritation.
 
We are also attaching a series of medical journal articles relating to contact dermatitis suffered by workers who were repetitively exposed to benzidine dyes. If you have any further questions about whether this exposure to benzidine dye caused the infection and sepsis in our client please feel free to reach out to me.

A listing of all materials supplied to you is attached on an index.

Very truly yours,
[REDACTED]
justification: The consumer died from sepsis caused by an infection from contact dermatitis due to toxic dyes in the shoes. The infection led to multiple amputations before death.
